text: What this is about A small rectangular battery is labeled 9 V. This figure is a voltage . It does not say how much energy the battery contains, but how much energy each unit of charge gives up as it passes from one terminal to the other 9 joules per coulomb. Charge is the property of certain particles of exerting and feeling electric forces. The joule is the unit of energy, the coulomb the unit of charge. The question of this chapter is Why is voltage always a difference between two points, and what does it do to a charge? The answer leads through two concepts. An electric field determines, for every location, what force acts on a charge there. The potential determines, for every location, how much energy per coulomb a charge has there relative to a freely chosen zero point, the reference point . How to work with this chapter. text: The discipline of electrical engineering is the engineering science that moves electric charges in a controlled way in order to transmit energy and process information. A power plant, a motor, a wireless network and a processor all rest on the same process forces set charges in motion. Physics describes nature with measurable quantities and looks for the laws connecting them. The engineering sciences apply these laws, for example in components, circuits connections of components and power plants. All materials consist of atoms. An atom has a tiny nucleus of protons and neutrons , around which electrons move Fig. 1 abb 1 . Protons carry a positive charge, electrons a negative charge of exactly the same size, neutrons none. An atom contains as many protons as electrons; seen from outside, their charges cancel, and it is neutral . If it loses an electron, a positive charge is left over. An atom with a surplus charge is called an ion . Protons sit firmly in the nucleus and are 1836 times heavier than electrons, whereas outer electrons can be detached. That is why electrons are what moves in nearly all processes of electrical engineering. Diagram of an atom with three protons and three neutrons. Left, neutral three positive and three negative charges add up to zero. Right, one electron is missing the ion carries the charge . text: This stage settles the first question What is charge, how does a charged body come about, and what is conserved in the process? The idea. Frictional electricity, lightning as the discharge of separated charges through the air, and magnetism cannot be explained by mechanics. If a glass rod is rubbed with a silk cloth and a hard rubber rod with fur, the two rods attract each other, while two hard rubber rods repel Fig. 3 abb 3 . Rubbing creates nothing new; electrons change bodies. Different materials bind their outer electrons with different strength. At the points of contact, electrons pass to the material that binds them more strongly, and rubbing creates many such points. A body with an electron deficit is positively charged, one with an electron excess negatively. Top rubbing separates charge. Electrons pass from the glass to the silk and from the fur to the rubber. Bottom oppositely charged rods attract, like charged rods repel. A body with protons and electrons carries the charge The elementary charge is the smallest charge occurring freely. An electron carries , a proton . In a closed system, the sum of all charges stays constant conservation of charge . ⁠ How to read it Charge occurs only in multiples of ; one coulomb is elementary charges. Rubbed rods carry around 10 nC. Validity These steps are noticeable only for individual particles; even 1 nC is six billion electrons. In circuits, charge is therefore treated as a continuous quantity. Two bodies together carry . If an electron passes from 1 to 2, decreases by one and increases by one; the bracket stays the same. The charges “generated” by rubbing always add up to zero. The names are older than the electron. In 1733 DuFay distinguished vitreous and resinous electricity; around 1750 Franklin called one positive and the other negative. The Greek word for amber, elektron , gave the field its name. Conductors and insulators. In a conductor such as metal, at least one electron per atom can wander through the entire body. In an insulator such as glass or rubber, the electrons stay with their atoms. That is why charge on an insulator stays where it was produced, whereas on metal it spreads immediately. Sphere A nC lacks electrons. A plastic sphere of 1 g contains around electrons, so only one in is missing. ⁠ Limiting case For , . A neutral body does not contain little charge; it contains equal amounts of both signs. Because the signs were assigned before electrons were known. Franklin called rubbed glass positive; only much later did it turn out that glass loses electrons in the process. The convention stayed, so the electron carries negative charge. There is nothing special about this physically. After rubbing, a glass rod carries nC. How many electrons has it given up? What charge does the cloth carry if both were neutral beforehand? Two identical metal spheres carry nC and nC. They touch and are separated. What charge does each carry? How many electrons have moved across, and in which direction? a electrons. The cloth has taken them up and carries nC. b The total charge nC is conserved and divides evenly between identical spheres nC each. The negative sphere therefore gives electrons to the positive one.

text: Everything so far held for charges at rest. This stage shows what changes when charges move and magnetic fields change, and where path independence ends. The idea. For a long time, electricity and magnetism were regarded as separate fields. In 1820 Ørsted saw a compass needle deflect next to a current carrying wire moving charge produces a magnetic field . In 1831 Faraday reversed the idea a magnet that he moved in a coil , a wire wound into turns, produced a voltage at its ends. This is called induction . In 1864 Maxwell combined everything into electromagnetism . The mechanism of induction is a new field a changing magnetic field produces an electric field with closed lines, a curl field . On one round trip in it, a charge gains energy, and that ends the statement 6.2 arbeit im feld.html gl 6 2 . Left cross section of a wire; the current flows into the page. The magnetic field runs in circles around the wire, and compass needles align their red tips with it. Right a moving bar magnet changes the magnetic flux through the coil. As long as it moves, the meter shows the voltage . The direction of the magnetic field is given by the right hand rule the thumb points in the conventional current direction, the fingers in the direction of the field. The conventional current direction runs from plus to minus; the electrons in the wire move the opposite way Chapter 2 /wissen/en/elektrotechnik/1 semester/grundlagen der elektrotechnik/strom widerstand und kirchhoff/strom widerstand und kirchhoff.html . If the magnetic flux through a coil with turns changes, the following voltage arises between its ends ⁠ How to read it The magnetic flux measures how much magnetic field passes through the coil area, weber . Small coils carry microwebers to milliwebers. Only the change counts, not the flux itself. The law is a measurement result along one turn, the curl field supplies the voltage ; the turns are in series and their voltages add. The lowercase letter stands for a time dependent voltage. The minus sign says that a current driven by this voltage opposes the change in flux. Validity All turns must enclose the same flux. Faraday also showed induction without a magnet he wound two coils onto a ring and connected a battery to one and a galvanometer an early current meter to the other. It deflected only when switching on and off, because only then does the flux change. Maxwell's equations in words. The equations themselves need more mathematics, but their content fits into four sentences. The flux density here is the measure of the density of the field lines. Gauss's law for electric fields Charges are sources and sinks of the electric flux density. Gauss's law for magnetism The magnetic flux density has no sources; its lines are closed. Law of induction Changes of the magnetic flux in time lead to an electric curl field. Ampère's law Currents and changes of the electric field in time lead to a magnetic curl field. The magnet in Fig. 12 abb 12 changes the flux through the coil with uniformly by 0.2 mWb in 25 ms. The voltage is then constant V. During this time, the loop integral of around the flux is not zero, and the voltage between two points depends on which side of the flux the path runs. ⁠ Limiting cases For constant flux, ; a magnet at rest produces no voltage. In most circuits, the changing fluxes sit almost entirely in coils. Between the components the field stays practically curl free, which is why potentials and voltages remain the tool there. The potential of a location is the work per charge up to the reference point. In a curl field, that depends on the path. Two paths give two values, and the location would have no unique potential. A current is moving charge, measured as charge per time. A resistor is a component that slows this motion and converts its energy into heat. Ohm's law links voltage and current at a component. The node rule says that no current disappears at a junction. The mesh rule says that the voltages along a closed path add up to zero. In a metal, at least one electron per atom is no longer bound to its atom. The positive ions left behind form a regular crystal lattice . If a voltage is applied, there is a field in the wire. It accelerates every free electron against the field direction. Right model for the directed part of the velocity. It grows in the field up to and falls to zero at a collision. Its mean value is the drift velocity . This motion cancels on average, carries no current and is preserved in the collisions. Two things travel in the wire, and they must not be confused. The electrons drift slowly. The field, by contrast, spreads along the wire as an electromagnetic wave when the switch closes, in cables at around m/s. The electrons are already everywhere in the wire. Each one starts drifting as soon as the field front reaches it Fig. 3 abb 3 . After a few such transit times, the steady current flows in the whole circuit. text: So far, was a number from material and shape. A purchased component has a standardized value and a tolerance, and its resistance changes with temperature. The idea. Manufacturing scatters by a percentage. That is why the values on offer are graded so that successive values have the same percentage spacing. For temperature, decides heat changes either the mobility or the charge carrier density . Types of construction. Metal film or carbon film resistors carry a thin layer on a ceramic body. This is the usual design for 0.1 to 2 W, and the value is printed on them as a color code. Wire wound resistors withstand high power and temperature and are suited to small values. SMD resistors Surface Mounted Device are soldered directly onto the circuit board. They are very small, allow a high packing density, tolerate little power and, because they have no connecting wires, are suited to high frequencies. text: From now on, what counts is no longer what happens inside the component, but what can be measured at its terminals. That requires a term for the component and an agreement about signs. The idea. For calculating, it is enough to know how a component responds to voltage with current. The inside may be unknown. Signs are fixed beforehand with arrows, because the true directions are often not known before the calculation. The result then says whether reality follows the arrow. A two terminal element is a component that can be fully described by the current and voltage between its two terminals. In the steady state time independent , that is its characteristic curve . A black box is a system whose outward behavior is known but whose construction is unknown or unimportant. A network is an interconnection of two terminal elements. If the characteristic curve is a straight line through the origin, ⁠ How to read it Such a linear two terminal element is the ohmic resistor Fig. 4 das ohmsche gesetz aus feld und stoen.html abb 4 right, each straight line one value . Batteries and voltage sources also belong to the building blocks of linear networks, but their characteristic curve does not pass through the origin Chapter 5 /wissen/en/elektrotechnik/1 semester/grundlagen der elektrotechnik/quellen und ersatzquellen/quellen und ersatzquellen.html . For a nonlinear two terminal element such as the incandescent lamp Fig. 5 reale widerstande werte und temperatur.html abb 5 right , depends on the operating point, and 5.1 gl 5 1 does not hold there. The voltage arrow points from 1 to 2 and means Chapter 1 /wissen/en/elektrotechnik/1 semester/grundlagen der elektrotechnik/ladung feld und potenzial/ladung feld und potenzial.html . The current arrow counts positive charge in the direction of the arrow. In the passive sign convention PSC, load convention , the voltage and current arrows at a two terminal element point in the same direction; in the active sign convention ASC, generator convention , they point in opposite directions. For a resistor, ⁠ How to read it Both conventions are only agreements. The direction of both arrows can be chosen freely; that changes signs, never the physics. The usual choice is the PSC at a load and the ASC at a source, because then all numbers are positive in normal operation Fig. 6 abb 6 left . Why this fits In a load, positive charge runs from high to low potential and gives up energy; current and voltage have the same direction. In a source, it is lifted from low to high potential; current and voltage have opposite directions. In the PSC, therefore means that energy is absorbed; in the ASC, it means that energy is delivered. The conventional current direction is the direction in which positive charge would move outside the source from plus to minus. It corresponds to the current arrow at a load in the PSC. text: The first kind of equation What does the conservation of charge demand at a node? The idea. A node is a piece of wire. If more flows in than out, charge collects on it and its potential rises. This lowers the voltage across the incoming resistors and raises it across the outgoing ones. The inflow falls and the outflow rises until both are equal. This self regulation takes place in nanoseconds. It is the mechanism behind the rule the node settles at exactly the potential at which nothing is left stuck. The sum of all currents flowing into a node is zero at every instant. Equivalently, the sum of the incoming currents equals the sum of the outgoing currents For a network with nodes, of these equations are independent. ⁠ How to read it The arrows can be chosen freely. If all point toward the node, at least one of the currents must be negative, or all are zero. With mixed arrows, incoming ones count as positive and outgoing ones as negative. Validity The node must not store any appreciable charge. That holds as long as the currents change slowly compared with the equalization time. The derivation gives a number for this. text: What this is about Two metal plates with an insulator between them this component is called a capacitor . If you connect it to a battery, current flows in the leads even though the plates do not touch. The current grows weaker and stops by itself. If you disconnect the battery, the voltage remains, and the component can drive current on its own. The question of this chapter is How can current flow into an insulator, why does it end by itself, and where is the energy afterward? Each plate is an electrode ; the insulator between them is called the dielectric . The quantity that characterizes the component is the capacitance it says how much charge sits on the plates per volt. The basic form is two flat plates, the parallel plate capacitor . text: The plates do not touch. Nevertheless, a meter in the lead shows current. This stage clarifies which charge moves where. The idea. The uncharged pair of plates is connected to the battery by wires Fig. 1 abb 1 . At the first moment both plates are at the same potential, but the battery terminals are 9 V apart. The potential drop therefore lies along the wires. There is a field there, and it pushes the free electrons in the metal. In the wire at plate A they run away from the plate to the plus terminal, in the wire at plate B from the minus terminal onto the plate. A loses electrons and becomes positive, B gains electrons and becomes negative. No electron crosses the gap every electron that arrives on B comes from the wire before it, not from A. With every displaced charge, the field between the plates grows and with it the voltage. The plates approach the potential of their terminals, the drop along the wires shrinks, the current decreases. At 9 V between the plates, each plate is at the potential of its terminal. No drop remains along the wires, no force acts on the electrons any more, and the current ends. text: A capacitor does not let charge through, it displaces it electrons leave one plate and arrive on the other, and the same current flows at both terminals at the same moment. The separated charge produces the field between the plates. This field determines the voltage , and it holds the field energy , stored in the space between the plates. Charge needs current and time, so the voltage does not jump. At the first moment an empty capacitor acts like a short circuit current at 0 V , a full one like an open circuit voltage without current . text: Before an error can be calculated, it must be clear what a meter is electrically a component with two terminals and a resistance between them. The idea. In a pointer instrument, a rotatable coil of thin wire sits between the poles of a permanent magnet Fig. 1 abb 1 . When current flows, the magnetic field exerts a force on the moving electrons in the wire, and the coil turns against a spiral spring. The torque grows with the current, the counterforce of the spring with the angle. That is why the deflection is proportional to the current. Two things cannot be avoided without current there is no deflection, and with current a voltage drops across the wire. text: Some networks contain no groups. Symmetry then supplies nodes of equal potential, and connecting them creates groups. The idea. If two nodes are at the same potential, the voltage between them is zero. A wire between them therefore carries no current, and nothing changes if you add it. Conversely, you may cut a current free branch. Symmetry reveals which nodes these are, without any calculation. For a network of resistors with the terminals A and B If mirroring or rotating maps the network onto itself while A and B stay in place, nodes that coincide have the same potential. You may connect them. A resistor between them carries no current. If mirroring maps the network onto itself while A and B swap places, every point on the mirror axis is at the mean value . text: What has been missing so far is whatever drives the current. This stage introduces the two basic building blocks that bring energy into a network. The idea. A source holds a single quantity fixed. The connected network determines the other. An ideal voltage source holds the potential difference between its terminals. The load decides what current flows. An ideal current source holds the current in its branch. The load likewise decides what voltage arises. Both are models. They cannot be built, but a regulated power supply or a transistor circuit Chapter 10 /wissen/en/elektrotechnik/1 semester/grundlagen der elektrotechnik/der bipolartransistor/der bipolartransistor.html comes close to them within a limited range. Left, the ideal voltage source in the diagram a horizontal line, the voltage does not depend on the current. Right, the ideal current source a vertical line, the current does not depend on the voltage. The stroke in the circuit symbol shows the behavior at the value zero drawn along the line, the line is closed; drawn across it, the line is interrupted. For the ideal voltage source and the ideal current source, ⁠ How to read it is the source voltage in V, from millivolts to kilovolts, here 9 V. is the source current in A, from microamperes to amperes. In Fig. 5 abb 5 the slope of the characteristic curve is the internal resistance with a negative sign zero for the voltage source, infinite for the current source. In calculations, a voltage source replaces the difference of two node potentials by a known value, and a current source fixes the current of a branch. ⁠ Validity Two connections contradict the model. A short circuited voltage source would have to satisfy both and . An open current source would have to satisfy both and , because a current needs a closed path. The 9 V source delivers 0.5625 A into 16 , 9 A into 1 , and it would be 9000 A into 1 m . A 0.5 A source produces 8 V across 16 , 500 V across 1 k , and it would be 500 kV across 1 M . ⁠ Limiting case The more extreme the load, the further the model departs from any real device. That is the reason for the next stage. Yes. An ideal source fixes only its one quantity. If the current flows into the plus terminal of a voltage source, then , and the source absorbs power. That is how a rechargeable battery is charged. In series with an ideal current source, a resistor is invisible from outside. c Nothing changes at the load; it stays at 5 V and 5 mA. The source delivers 505 mA instead of 5 mA. In parallel with an ideal voltage source, a resistor is invisible from outside.

In series, the same current flows through both sources, and their terminal voltages add at every current. In parallel, the same voltage lies across both, and their currents add at every voltage. That is why you calculate the series connection in the voltage source form and the parallel connection in the current source form. Two straight lines again give a straight line, and hence again a real source. text: When there are several sources at different places in the network, groups alone do not help. The superposition method splits the problem into one calculation per source. The idea. A network is determined by three kinds of equations node rule, mesh rule, Ohm's law. None of them contains a product or a square of currents and voltages, as long as is fixed. Such equations are linear. If such a system has the solution for one source and the solution for another, then is the solution when both sources act at the same time. Substitution shows this every equation adds term by term. So each source drives its own current through the network as if the other were not there, and the currents add in every branch. In a linear network with independent voltage sources and independent current sources, every branch voltage and every branch current satisfies The coefficients depend only on the resistors, not on the sources. ⁠ How to read it A source is independent if its value depends on no quantity in the network. is the voltage gain from source to the voltage , without a unit this is how many volts changes per volt of the source. It is also called the sensitivity . in is the transfer resistance the transimpedance from a current source to this voltage. Correspondingly, in S and the current gain describe the current between two nodes C and D. and stand for any voltage and any current in the network. Validity only for linear networks and only for voltages and currents. The procedure. Turn off all sources except one. An ideal voltage source with the value zero forces equal potentials at its terminals, which is what a wire does it becomes a short circuit . An ideal current source with the value zero forces the current zero, which is what a gap does it becomes open terminals . Internal resistances of real sources stay in the network. text: In a linear network the effects of the sources add up, because all the equations are linear. This is superposition , the overlaying of effects. Therefore the voltage at two terminals A and B is a straight line in the terminal current . The sources set the open circuit voltage the voltage with the terminals open , the resistors set the internal resistance the slope . A straight line has two numbers. So the network behaves like an equivalent source , a source with an internal resistance. The open circuit and the short circuit terminals connected supply the numbers . Series add resistances, same current. Parallel add conductances, same voltage. Combine from the inside out. Nodes of equal potential may be connected, current free branches may be cut. Symmetry shows where this is possible. Star and delta are interchangeable at the terminals . Ideal sources hold one quantity fixed. Real sources . Converting , same resistance. Superposition voltage sources become wires, current sources become gaps, partial effects add. Powers do not add. Every linear one port is a straight line , , . The operating point is the intersection with the line of the load. One principle behind all the results. At two terminals a linear network behaves like a single straight line in the current voltage diagram, which is why two numbers are enough. text: A network with four terminals has three independent currents and three independent voltages. This stage shows which condition turns these into two currents and two voltages. The idea. A four pole is a network with four terminals. The node rule Chapter 2 /wissen/en/elektrotechnik/1 semester/grundlagen der elektrotechnik/strom widerstand und kirchhoff/strom widerstand und kirchhoff.html holds for the whole network as for one large node One terminal current is fixed by the other three. The mesh rule likewise ties together the voltages between the terminals. Now if a two terminal element, say a source, is connected to terminals 1 and 1 , a further statement is added A two terminal element has only two connections. Every charge it gives off at one it takes back at the other. The current that enters the network at terminal 1 must return at terminal 1 . The terminal pair behaves like a single access with one current and one voltage Fig. 1 abb 1 left . At a four pole with the terminals 1, 1 , 2, 2 , let all terminal currents be counted toward the network. It always holds that A terminal pair is a port if the port condition holds. A four pole with two ports is a two port Its port quantities are , , and . ⁠ How to read it 1.1 gl 1 1 leaves three currents and three voltages free. The first equation is the node rule, the second the mesh rule around the loop . 1.2 gl 1 2 removes one current each. The voltage also drops out of the description No current flows between the ports on the outside, so no power is transferred through it. Whether a four pole becomes a two port is decided by what is connected to it If a two terminal element is connected to each terminal pair, 1.2 gl 1 2 holds automatically. A branch running outside from port to port breaks it Fig. 1 abb 1 right . The historical name four pole lives on in four pole theory . Left source, two port and load. At both ports, each current returns at the second terminal, and energy flows in the forward direction from port 1 to port 2. Right An external branch from terminal 1 to terminal 2 carries the current . Now a different current flows into 1 than out of 1 , and the terminal pairs are no longer ports. A two port is a conceptually closed unit, accessible only through its ports. Its properties are fixed by the relations between the port quantities, and these can be calculated or measured. Usually a source is connected to port 1, the input , and a load to port 2, the output . Energy then flows in the forward direction ; the opposite direction is called the reverse direction . The two port is a basic structure Controlled sources are two ports, transformers, amplifiers and transistors have three or four connections, large two ports can be built from elementary two ports , and two ports joined together form a two port again. The simplest examples are the voltage divider and the current divider Chapter 2 /wissen/en/elektrotechnik/1 semester/grundlagen der elektrotechnik/strom widerstand und kirchhoff/strom widerstand und kirchhoff.html . Structure and classification. If a two port has a continuous line from terminal 1 to 2 , the ground line , it is called unbalanced Fig. 2 abb 2 left . It is really a three pole, an improper four pole. Network models of transistors and amplifiers are of this kind. A two port that, like the bridge circuit, has no such line and is built as a mirror image about a center line is called balanced . By their behavior, two ports are divided into linear time invariant, time varying and nonlinear ones. This chapter deals with the linear time invariant ones. text: Four port quantities are four unknowns. This stage shows why the two port contributes exactly two equations and why they contain only four numbers. The idea. Source and load each supply one equation between the voltage and the current of their port. Two are missing, and the two port supplies them. If you specify two port quantities, say both currents, all the currents and voltages inside are fixed, and so are the other two port quantities. The specified quantities are the causes, the others the effects. If the two port is linear and contains no independent sources, superposition from Chapter 5 /wissen/en/elektrotechnik/1 semester/grundlagen der elektrotechnik/quellen und ersatzquellen/quellen und ersatzquellen.html applies Each effect is the sum of the part due to the first cause and the part due to the second cause, each part proportional to its cause. Two effects times two causes give four factors. A time invariant two port is completely described by two two port functions , for example If it is linear and free of independent sources, then for effects and causes ⁠ How to read it The first digit of a parameter names the effect, the second the cause. The parameters depend only on the two port, not on source or load. Four quantities can be split into two causes and two effects in six ways. The four forms of this chapter are the usual ones. Validity 2.1 gl 2 1 also holds for nonlinear two ports, then as curves. For the transistor, this describes either the behavior for DC quantities or the signal behavior for small AC quantities. A transformer with separate windings transmits only time varying quantities. 2.2 gl 2 2 requires linearity. Reference arrows. To make the signs unique, a convention is needed Fig. 3 abb 3 . In the symmetric arrow system , also called the mathematical sign convention, the passive sign convention from Chapter 2 /wissen/en/elektrotechnik/1 semester/grundlagen der elektrotechnik/strom widerstand und kirchhoff/strom widerstand und kirchhoff.html applies at both ports The current arrows point into the two port. In the chain arrow system , also called the technical arrow system, it applies only at the input; at the output the active sign convention applies The output current points out, toward the load. This chapter uses the mixed arrow system and always point in. Where the chain form needs the current flowing out, it writes it explicitly as . A load therefore gives a negative in normal operation. The three arrow systems. Left, symmetric Both currents point into the two port. Center, chain arrows The output current points toward the load. Right, mixed, as in this chapter stays defined as on the left, and the current to the load is called . At the center point of the T two port, and meet, and their sum flows through . text: What this is about A charger turns the AC voltage of the wall outlet into the DC voltage for the rechargeable battery. The component that does this is called a diode it lets current through in one direction forward direction and blocks it in the other reverse direction . It consists of a semiconductor , a material whose conductivity lies between that of a metal and that of an insulator and can be set deliberately. The question of this chapter is How does a piece of silicon become a valve for current, and how do you calculate with a component that does not obey Ohm's law? The answer runs through six terms. Doping means building in a few foreign atoms, which fixes how many charge carriers mobile charges the crystal has. At the boundary between two differently doped regions, the pn junction , the space charge region forms by itself, a thin layer without mobile charges that acts as an energy barrier. The characteristic curve is the graph of current versus voltage, the operating point the pair of voltage and current that settles in a circuit. How to work with this chapter. text: Metal conducts, glass does not, pure silicon hardly at all. The difference lies in the number of mobile electrons. This stage explains it from the allowed energies in the crystal. The idea. In a single atom, electrons have only certain energies, the energy levels . In a crystal regular lattice of atoms the shells overlap, and the electrons belong to the whole crystal. No two electrons may occupy the same state. That is why each level splits into as many closely spaced levels as the crystal has atoms. This creates a band of allowed energies. Between the bands lies the forbidden zone there are no states there. A field can accelerate an electron only if a free state lies just above it. So a full band does not conduct, no matter how many electrons it contains. Band model, not to scale; is the energy of an electron. In the metal, the top band is only partly filled. In the semiconductor, heat lifts a few electrons over the small gap and leaves holes behind. In the insulator, the gap is too large. The valence band VB is the top band that is fully occupied at . The conduction band CB lies above it and is empty at . The band gap is the smallest energy that lifts an electron from the VB into the CB. The Fermi energy separates occupied from empty states at . At it is the energy at which a state would be occupied half of the time; it may lie in the gap even though there is no state there. ⁠ How to read it Silicon has eV, germanium 0.67 eV, diamond 5.5 eV. Three cases In a metal , the top occupied band is only partly filled, free states lie directly above the electrons, and it conducts at every temperature. In an insulator , is so large that no electron gets across. A semiconductor is an insulator with a small gap at it insulates; when excited by heat, light or strong fields, electrons get into the CB. An electron that moves into the CB leaves a free place in the VB. A neighboring electron moves in, and the place wanders. The hole defect electron behaves like a mobile particle with the charge . Both count as charge carriers electrons in the CB and holes in the VB. If an electron falls back into a hole, both disappear; this is called recombination . text: An n piece and a p piece are, on their own, just resistors. This stage shows what forms at their boundary and why it is a barrier. The idea. In a crystal, a p region borders an n region. Four steps take place Fig. 4 abb 4 ⁠ Diffusion. Charge carriers move randomly. More of them wander out of the region of high density than into it. This equalization by random motion is called diffusion . Electrons wander from the n region into the p region, holes the other way. ⁠ Recombination. In the foreign region the wanderers meet the majority there and disappear. Near the boundary, hardly any free carriers remain afterward. ⁠ Fixed ions remain. There the ions are no longer balanced on the n side, on the p side. This stationary charge is called space charge , the layer the space charge region. ⁠ The field stops the equalization. The ions create a field from the n side to the p side. It drives electrons back into the n region and holes back into the p region drift , Chapter 2 /wissen/en/elektrotechnik/1 semester/grundlagen der elektrotechnik/strom widerstand und kirchhoff/strom widerstand und kirchhoff.html . The region grows until the drift current exactly cancels the diffusion current. pn junction without external voltage. Top boxes are fixed ions, filled circles electrons, open circles holes. In the region the mobile carriers are missing, and the field points to the p side. Bottom the potential rises only in the region, by V in total. text: At the pn junction, mobile charges move into the other region and leave fixed ions behind. The field of these ions builds up a barrier in the space charge region that stops the equalization. Heat lifts only the fraction of the charge carriers over a barrier of height . Voltage in the forward direction lowers the barrier, so the current grows exponentially, by a factor of 10 per 60 mV . In the reverse direction only the tiny current remains. In a circuit, the operating point lies at the intersection of the characteristic curve and the load line the straight line set by source and resistor . For hand calculations the diode becomes a switch with a fixed forward voltage, and for small changes around the operating point it becomes a resistor . text: What this is about A microphone delivers millivolts, a loudspeaker needs volts. A computer output delivers milliamperes, a motor needs amperes. Between them sits a component that controls a large current with a small signal. The classic representative is the bipolar transistor , a semiconductor component made of three layers with three terminals. The energy comes from the supply voltage; the signal only sets the amount. The other important type, the MOSFET, dominates digital electronics and is not the subject of this chapter. text: In n doped silicon, electrons are free to move; in p doped silicon, holes are missing electrons that move like positive charges. At the boundary between the two regions, the pn junction , the space charge region forms a strip with almost no free carriers, in which fixed ions produce an electric field from the n region to the p region. This field acts as a barrier for the majority carriers of each side. Plus at the p region lowers it, and the diode conducts in the forward direction . Plus at the n region raises it, and the diode blocks. Diffusion is the motion of particles from a dense place to a sparse one; recombination is the encounter of an electron with a hole, in which both disappear as free carriers. For the diode follows the equation , and at the operating point one calculates with the tangent to its characteristic curve.

An npn transistor consists of three regions of the same semiconductor n doped emitter, p doped base, n doped collector Fig. 1 abb 1 . text: The CB diode blocks, and yet milliamperes flow through it. This stage follows the path of the electrons and shows why only a small base current is needed. The idea. A blocking diode does not block because its boundary is impermeable. It blocks because almost no free electrons are available on the p side. The field of the space charge region drives every electron that reaches the boundary from the p side across into the n region. For such electrons the boundary is a steep drop Fig. 2 abb 2 , bottom . The transistor supplies exactly these missing electrons, in four steps ⁠ Injection. lowers the barrier at the BE boundary. Electrons from the emitter enter the base. This introduction is called injection . The electron density at the emitter edge of the base grows with . ⁠ Crossing. In the p type base, electrons are a minority among many holes. They diffuse to the collector edge, where their density is almost zero. The base is much narrower than the diffusion length , the mean distance until recombination, several tens of µ m. That is why almost all of them get through. ⁠ Sweeping out. At the collector edge, the field of the CB boundary catches every arriving electron and pulls it into the collector. How large is hardly matters; the field always collects them all. That is why hardly depends on . ⁠ Replenishing. Two small losses remain holes from the base pass into the emitter, and some electrons recombine in the base. Both use up holes. The base terminal must replace them. This replacement is the base current. It stays small because the emitter is much more heavily doped than the base and because the base is so narrow. The electrons run from the emitter to the collector. text: With exponential functions, circuits can hardly be solved by hand. This stage replaces the surface with three linear pieces. The idea. Each of the two diodes can conduct or block. This gives the operating states. If the BE diode blocks, no electron starts and nothing flows. This is the cut off region . If it conducts and the CB diode blocks, the collector collects all the electrons, and holds. This is the active region. If falls so far that the CB diode conducts noticeably as well, the collector sends electrons back. Then it can no longer collect them all, the base fills up with electrons, and stays below . This is the saturation region . text: What this is about An operational amplifier , op amp for short, is an integrated amplifier made of a few dozen transistors. It amplifies the voltage between its two inputs by a factor of about 100000. This factor is called the open loop gain . It varies by a factor of four from one specimen to the next and changes with temperature. Nevertheless, this component is used to build amplifiers that feel only 0.01 % of this variation, as well as summing amplifiers and integrators. The question is How does a huge, imprecise factor turn into a component whose behavior is determined by the resistors alone? The answer is negative feedback part of the output voltage is fed back to the input in such a way that it counteracts its own cause. How to work with this chapter. text: A sensor delivers millivolts, and every conductor produces a random interference voltage. This stage clarifies where it comes from, how it is measured, and what an amplifier can do about it. The idea. Noise is a disturbance made up of many oscillations of different frequency and amplitude. Its waveform is random and can only be described statistically the mean is zero, and the rms value measures its strength. Because independent disturbances sometimes reinforce and sometimes cancel each other, it is not their rms values that add but the squares of these values. That is why noise is described by the noise voltage density the contribution of each frequency strip 1 Hz wide to the square of the rms value. The rms value of the noise voltage and the density of the thermal noise of a resistor are The signal to noise ratio is the ratio of the powers, written in decibels dB ⁠ How to read it . J/K is the Boltzmann constant it converts temperature into mean thermal energy per particle. is the absolute temperature in K, the resistance. is the base 10 logarithm. 20 dB mean a factor of 10 in voltage and 100 in power. Validity The right hand part of 1.1 gl 1 1 holds up to far beyond the frequencies of electronics. | Type | Mechanism | Density | | | | | | Thermal noise | Thermal motion of the charge carriers in every conductor. Random accumulations at the ends produce a voltage, even without current flow. | constant, | | Shot noise | Current consists of individual charges that cross a potential barrier at random times, for example in the pn junction. | constant | | 1/f noise | Recharging of surface states, fluctuating number of free charge carriers in the semiconductor. | , interferes up to about 10 kHz | Constant density is called white noise , after white light made of all colors. This is a shape of the spectrum, not a cause. Integrated over all frequencies it would give infinite power. That is a limit of the model real densities fall off at very high frequencies, and every circuit has a finite bandwidth , the frequency range it passes. For white noise the integral becomes . Right, the same useful signal without noise and with noise at 20 dB, that is, at a tenth of its rms value. For two independent disturbances, . Averaged over time, the product is positive as often as it is negative, so its mean vanishes. What remains is . The integral in 1.1 gl 1 1 is this sum over all frequency strips. The sensor resistor has , so in 20 kHz, µ V. The useful signal of 1 mV is 549 times larger dB. Half the bandwidth lowers the noise by , which is 3 dB. ⁠ Limiting cases For or the thermal noise vanishes. What an amplifier changes. It raises the signal and the noise present at its input by the same factor, so the SNR stays the same or gets worse through the amplifier's own noise. It helps only against disturbances that join in behind it and have a fixed size. If the line to the next device adds 100 µ V, then 20.0 dB remain without an amplifier. With a gain of 100 at the sensor it is , that is, 53.7 dB. The second remedy is the difference a disturbance that hits two lines equally vanishes if only their difference is evaluated. ft_text: what must be assumed about numbers and why the square root of 2 is not a fraction what this is about school teaches rules like or “you must not divide by zero.” why do they hold? habit as a justification does not get you far for complex numbers chapter 2 /wissen/en/elektrotechnik/1 semester/hohere mathematik 1/komplexe zahlen/komplexe zahlen.html the rule “squares are not negative” fails, and all limits chapter 4 depend on a property of the numbers that school never mentions. you can see it in a single number the diagonal of a square with side length 1 has length , and no fraction has this value. the question of this chapter is what exactly must be assumed about numbers so that all the rules of arithmetic become provable, and what distinguishes the real numbers from the fractions? text: What this is about A system takes in one signal and puts out another an RC circuit smooths a voltage, a loudspeaker cabinet colors a sound, a measuring amplifier delays and amplifies. The question of this chapter is What do you need to know about a system to compute its output for any input signal? text: Stage 1 warum gerade.html stufe 1 applies to a single building block. It becomes useful only if every signal can be built from building blocks . This stage shows that this works, what the weights are called and where the limits lie. Starting point pure oscillations On the imaginary axis the building blocks are pure oscillations . An absolutely integrable signal , so it decays fast enough on both sides can be built from them. This is the Fourier representation . Its formula is all that is needed here. The function is called the spectrum ; it gives the weight of the oscillation with frequency For many signals in system theory this is not enough. The step does not decay, and the impulse response of an unstable system even grows. A signal that grows without bound cannot be built from oscillations of constant amplitude.

text: What kinds of signals are there, and how is sampling described mathematically? Four classes. Time and amplitude can each be continuous or discrete. An analog signal is continuous in both. A discrete time signal has values only at the times , but these with arbitrary precision. A digital signal is in addition stepped in amplitude quantized , because a computer can represent only finitely many numbers. This chapter deals with the discretization of time. The quantization of the amplitude is a separate topic. From the real to the ideal sampler. In every clock cycle, a real sampler closes a switch for the short time If is made shorter and shorter, only the values remain. Mathematically, the rectangle is replaced by a Dirac impulse. This is the ideal sampler The sampled signal is a train of Dirac impulses, each with a sample as its weight. The second step is the sifting property . In this form, sampled signals can be treated with all the tools for continuous signals.

text: How do you describe a signal whose waveform you do not know? You imagine many signals of the same kind and average over them. The idea. If you measure the noise of many identically built resistors at the same temperature, you get many different curves , Fig. 1 abb 1 . Each one is called a sample function or realization. The imagined totality of all of them is called a random process . The values of all sample functions at a fixed instant form a random variable . ⁠ How to read it is called the expected value or ensemble average you average over all sample functions at the same instant, that is, vertically in Fig. 1 abb 1 . With you obtain the mean square value. The autocorrelation function averages the product of the values at two instants. It tells you how strongly the value at is related to the value at . text: What this is about A calculator computes exactly what you are typing in at the moment. If you want the same calculation for twenty prices, you type it twenty times, and each time a typo can happen. A program, on the other hand, computes what you have written down for it once as often as you like, with as many numbers as you like and without new typos, once it is correct. This chapter explores how to write down such a list of instructions for a computer and how to get the computer to carry it out. By the end, Python runs on your own computer, on Windows or on Linux. You can use it to calculate, write and start small programs, and you can read the messages with which Python points out errors. How to work with this chapter. ft_text: a computer does only what it is told to do, step by step. a computer does only what it is told to do, step by step. this section explains what a program is, which instructions the processor of a computer understands, and why programs are written down in a language of their own. the program a computer can calculate very fast, but it decides nothing on its own. before it does anything useful, someone has to tell it exactly which steps to carry out and in which order. a recipe. a cooking recipe is such a sequence of steps “bring water to a boil. add the pasta. wait nine minutes. drain.” whoever follows it does not need to know why pasta needs nine minutes. they only need to understand each step unambiguously and keep to the order. knowing what something is, and knowing how to find it. the sentence “the square root of 2 is the positive number that, multiplied by itself, gives 2” describes completely. but it does not say how to find this number. a recipe that delivers the number step by step is knowledge of a different kind it describes a method. a computer can only do something with knowledge of this second kind. a program is a sequence of unambiguously described steps that a computer carries out one after another, without asking questions. a single step of a program is called a statement . the following recipe is called heron's method, after heron of alexandria, who described it in the first century. it needs only the basic arithmetic operations choose a first estimate , for example . compute and form the mean . this mean is the new estimate . repeat step 2 until no longer changes in the digits you are interested in. by hand with a calculator, you get | pass | | | new estimate | | | | | | | 1 | | | | | 2 | | | | | 3 | | | | | 4 | | | | after three passes, and ; after four passes, the first six decimal places agree with . figure 1 abb 1 shows what happens and always lie on different sides of , and their mean moves closer each time. heron's method for on the number line. in each pass, the estimate blue and orange lie on different sides of , because their product is 2. their mean tick mark becomes the new estimate. the distance between the two points shrinks from via to ; in the third pass, they almost coincide in this picture. whoever follows the recipe does not need to know why it works. every step is so unambiguous that even a machine can carry it out. that is exactly what turns a recipe into a program. ⁠ in short a program is a recipe of unambiguous steps that a computer can carry out without asking back. if an estimate is too large, , then is too small, because the product is always 2. the root therefore lies between and , and the mean of the two is a reasonable next try. a short calculation shows how fast this goes. for the new estimate , two things follow from this the right hand side is never negative. from the first pass on, every estimate is therefore at least as large as , and lies below it. the error is squared in every pass and additionally divided by , that is, from the second pass on by at least 8. starting with , is successively , then , then , then . the number of correct digits roughly doubles in each pass. if you know newton's method from mathematics heron's method is newton's method for the zero of . its step is exactly . what the processor understands machine instructions in a computer, the steps of a program are carried out by the processor , a chip that calculates and controls the sequence of steps. its instructions are much simpler than “form the mean of and ”. a very literal worker. you can picture the processor as an extremely fast worker with a tiny vocabulary. it understands instructions such as “fetch the number from memory cell 12”, “add two numbers”, “divide two numbers” or “continue at instruction 3”. it cannot do more than that, but it manages billions of these every second. the picture is only an aid to imagination; the processor understands nothing in the human sense, but carries out its instructions mechanically. a machine instruction is an instruction that the processor can carry out directly. it is stored in memory as a number; from this number the processor recognizes what to do. a program that consists only of machine instructions is called machine code . step 2 of heron's recipe breaks down into machine instructions roughly like this text: A computer does only what it is told to do, step by step. This section explains what a program is, which instructions the processor of a computer understands, and why programs are written down in a language of their own. The program A computer can calculate very fast, but it decides nothing on its own. Before it does anything useful, someone has to tell it exactly which steps to carry out and in which order. A recipe. A cooking recipe is such a sequence of steps “Bring water to a boil. Add the pasta. Wait nine minutes. Drain.” Whoever follows it does not need to know why pasta needs nine minutes. They only need to understand each step unambiguously and keep to the order. Knowing what something is, and knowing how to find it. The sentence “The square root of 2 is the positive number that, multiplied by itself, gives 2” describes completely. But it does not say how to find this number. A recipe that delivers the number step by step is knowledge of a different kind it describes a method. A computer can only do something with knowledge of this second kind. A program is a sequence of unambiguously described steps that a computer carries out one after another, without asking questions. A single step of a program is called a statement . The following recipe is called Heron's method, after Heron of Alexandria, who described it in the first century. It needs only the basic arithmetic operations Choose a first estimate , for example . Compute and form the mean . This mean is the new estimate . Repeat step 2 until no longer changes in the digits you are interested in. By hand with a calculator, you get | Pass | | | new estimate | | | | | | | 1 | | | | | 2 | | | | | 3 | | | | | 4 | | | | After three passes, and ; after four passes, the first six decimal places agree with . Figure 1 abb 1 shows what happens and always lie on different sides of , and their mean moves closer each time. Heron's method for on the number line. In each pass, the estimate blue and orange lie on different sides of , because their product is 2. Their mean tick mark becomes the new estimate. The distance between the two points shrinks from via to ; in the third pass, they almost coincide in this picture. Whoever follows the recipe does not need to know why it works. Every step is so unambiguous that even a machine can carry it out. That is exactly what turns a recipe into a program. ⁠ In short A program is a recipe of unambiguous steps that a computer can carry out without asking back. If an estimate is too large, , then is too small, because the product is always 2. The root therefore lies between and , and the mean of the two is a reasonable next try. A short calculation shows how fast this goes. For the new estimate , Two things follow from this The right hand side is never negative. From the first pass on, every estimate is therefore at least as large as , and lies below it. The error is squared in every pass and additionally divided by , that is, from the second pass on by at least 8. Starting with , is successively , then , then , then . The number of correct digits roughly doubles in each pass. If you know Newton's method from mathematics Heron's method is Newton's method for the zero of . Its step is exactly . What the processor understands machine instructions In a computer, the steps of a program are carried out by the processor , a chip that calculates and controls the sequence of steps. Its instructions are much simpler than “form the mean of and ”. A very literal worker. You can picture the processor as an extremely fast worker with a tiny vocabulary. It understands instructions such as “fetch the number from memory cell 12”, “add two numbers”, “divide two numbers” or “continue at instruction 3”. It cannot do more than that, but it manages billions of these every second. The picture is only an aid to imagination; the processor understands nothing in the human sense, but carries out its instructions mechanically. A machine instruction is an instruction that the processor can carry out directly. It is stored in memory as a number; from this number the processor recognizes what to do. A program that consists only of machine instructions is called machine code . Step 2 of Heron's recipe breaks down into machine instructions roughly like this Fetch the number from memory. Divide 2 by this number. Add to the result. Divide the result by 2. Store the result in memory as the new . Each of these instructions is a number in memory. Which number means which instruction is defined differently for each family of processors. The processors of most PCs understand different numbers than those of a smartphone. Machine code for one therefore does not run on the other. ⁠ In short The processor understands only very simple machine instructions, which are stored as numbers in memory, and each processor family has its own. Every machine instruction is permanently built into the processor chip. One part of the processor, the arithmetic unit, adds two numbers, for example. Another part, the control unit, reads the number of the next instruction and connects the matching parts with each other, such as “memory cell 12 to the input of the arithmetic unit, result back to memory”. The fewer and simpler the instructions, the smaller, faster and more economical the chip can be built. Everything complicated arises from many simple instructions running one after another, just as you can build a whole castle from a few kinds of Lego bricks. The processor always runs through the same cycle fetch the instruction, decode the instruction, execute the instruction, move on to the next instruction. The programming language Machine code is a long sequence of numbers. People can hardly read it, and it applies to only one processor family. A recipe in everyday language would be more convenient, but everyday language is ambiguous. Ambiguity. “I saw the man with the binoculars.” Did I have the binoculars, or did the man? A person guesses the intended meaning from the context. A computer cannot do that; it needs exactly one meaning for every sentence. A programming language is an artificial language in which it is precisely defined which texts are allowed and what each allowed text does. Python, C and C++ are programming languages. In Python, you write the first pass of Heron's recipe with like this The character / means “divided by”, + means “plus”, and the parentheses work as in mathematics. In Python, this line has exactly one meaning divide 2 by 1, add 1, divide the result by 2. ⁠ In short A programming language is an artificial language without ambiguity in which programs are written down. Syntax With a programming language, two questions have to be kept apart Is a text allowed at all? And what does it do? The first question concerns only the form. Form without meaning. The sentence “The wulp blinks the graffel.” is grammatically well built subject, verb, object. It just means nothing. “Graffel the blinks wulp the.”, on the other hand, is wrong even in its form. Whether a sentence is well built can be checked without knowing its meaning. The syntax of a programming language is the set of all rules that determine which texts are allowed in it. In Python, 1 + 2 / 1 / 2 is allowed. The following lines violate the syntax 1 + 2 / 1 / 2 A parenthesis is opened and never closed. 1 + / 2 A number is missing between + and / . ⁠ In short The syntax determines the allowed form, regardless of what a text means. Semantics A text in an allowed form must also have a defined effect. The semantics of a programming language determines what an allowed text means, that is, what happens when it is run. The line 7 / 2 is allowed in Python and in C, so it has the correct form in both languages. In Python it means “divide 7 by 2”, and the result is 3.5. In C, with whole numbers, the same text means “divide and drop the remainder”, and the result is 3. Same form, different meaning. A second example if you want to compute the mean of 3 and 4 and write 3 + 4 / 2 , you have written an allowed text. But its defined meaning is , not the intended mean . The semantics follows the text, not the intention. ⁠ In short The semantics determines what an allowed text does. The syntax of Python is written down as a formal grammar a list of rules such as “an expression in parentheses is an opening parenthesis, then an expression, then a closing parenthesis”. It is given in full in the Python Language Reference. The program that runs Python texts contains a part that is generated from exactly this grammar and checks every text against its rules. The semantics, by contrast, is described in words for every allowed form, the language reference says what it does. Source code What a person writes down in a programming language needs a name to distinguish it from machine code. The source code of a program is its text in a programming language, the way people write and read it. The line 1 + 2 / 1 / 2 is a very short piece of Python source code. A processor cannot run it, because it understands only machine instructions. So something has to translate between the source code and the processor. ⁠ In short Source code is the program in the form in which people write it; the processor cannot run it directly. Start with and carry out three passes. Write down each time with six decimal places. Compute after each pass. How close is it to 10? In each pass, compare and . Which of the two numbers is larger? The gap shrinks drastically each time because, according to the Background box in Subsection 1.1 stufe 1 1 , it is squared and divided . c Before the first pass, is smaller than the starting estimate is too small. From then on, is always the larger number and . The reason the product is always 10, so always lies between the two numbers; and after one pass, is never too small again, as the Background box in Subsection 1.1 stufe 1 1 shows. For each case, decide whether the syntax is violated, whether an allowed text means something other than intended, or whether the text is ambiguous. In Python 3 + 4 / 2 . In Python, the mean of 3 and 4 is to be computed 3 + 4 / 2 . In Python 3 + 4 . A request “Photograph the woman with the camera.” A program in C contains 7 / 2 and is supposed to give 3.5. a Syntax violated the opened parenthesis is never closed. b An allowed text that means something other than intended. Python does multiplication and division before addition and subtraction, so . What was meant is 3 + 4 / 2 , with the value 3.5. c Syntax violated after + , a number is missing before follows. d Ambiguous is the woman holding a camera in her hand, or are you supposed to use the camera? A human asks back or decides from the context; in a programming language, there must be no such spot. e An allowed text that means something other than intended. Under the semantics of C, 7 / 2 with whole numbers gives 3, not 3.5. If you want 3.5 in C, you have to write at least one of the numbers with a decimal place, for instance 7.0 / 2 . The mean of three numbers , and that are stored in memory is to be computed and stored in memory. Break the calculation down into instructions of the kind “fetch a number from memory”, “add”, “divide by a number” and “store in memory”, as in the example in Subsection 1.2 stufe 1 2 . How many instructions do you need? Fetch each number only once. One possible sequence Fetch from memory. Fetch from memory. Add the two numbers; result . Fetch from memory. Add ; result . Divide the result by 3. Store the result in memory. These are seven instructions three for fetching, two additions, one division, one store. A single line of source code such as a + b + c / 3 therefore becomes several machine instructions. Exactly how many depends on the processor family; some processors, for example, can fetch a number from memory and add it in the same instruction.

text: The processor understands only machine code; people write source code. This section shows the two basic ways of closing this gap, and which way Python takes. The compiler Source code has to be translated into machine code. A program can take on this job. A book translator. A book is translated completely once, then printed and sold. The readers of the translation no longer need the translator; they hold a finished book in their hands. A compiler is a program that translates a source code completely into machine code before that code is run. The result is saved as a separate file that runs without the compiler. Such a file is called an executable file . On Windows, its name usually ends in .exe . Programs in the C language are translated this way. From the source code hallo.c , the compiler gcc produces the executable file hallo.exe Windows or hallo Linux . You then start this file directly, as often as you like and without the compiler. It contains machine code for a particular processor family and a particular operating system; for a different computer, you have to translate again. ⁠ In short A compiler translates the whole source code once, in advance, into an executable file of machine code. The interpreter It also works without an executable file a program can read the source code and itself do what it says. A human interpreter. In a conversation between two languages, an interpreter sits in and translates while people are speaking. No written result is produced; at the next conversation, the interpreter has to be there again. The picture captures the role of an interpreter program, not every detail of how it works. An interpreter is a program that reads a source code and itself carries out the steps described in it. It produces no executable file and therefore has to be present every time the program is started. Python programs run this way. You start the source code hallo.py with a command such as python hallo.py . The program python is the interpreter it reads the file and carries out what it says. All the while, the processor runs the machine code of the interpreter, never the Python source code itself. The two ways compared | | Compiler | Interpreter | | | | | | translation happens | once, before any start | at every start | | result | executable file | no file, only the effect | | what you pass on | the executable file | the source code; the recipient needs the interpreter | | runs on | the processor family and the operating system it was translated for | any computer for which the interpreter exists | | speed | fast | slower, because the interpreter does work at every step | ⁠ In short An interpreter runs the source code itself, without producing an executable file. An interpreter has two advantages that are decisive for Python. You can type in a line and immediately see what it does, without a translation step in between. And the same source code runs unchanged on Windows, Linux and macOS, on the processor of a PC as well as on the completely different processor of a newer Mac; only the interpreter itself has to exist for each system. The price is speed. At every step, the interpreter first has to do work of its own before the actual calculation happens. Computation heavy programs are therefore often written so that the heavy parts run in ready made, translated machine code that Python merely calls. Python and CPython The word “Python” refers to two different things a language and a program. Python is a programming language; its syntax and semantics are laid down in the Python Language Reference. CPython is the program that runs Python source code and is offered on python.org ; it is itself written in the C language. CPython is the original and by far the most widely used program of this kind. New language features usually appear there first. There are other programs that run Python source code, for example PyPy, which runs many programs faster. They follow the same language reference, that is, the same syntax and semantics. In this series, the program python always means CPython. ⁠ In short Python is the language; CPython is the program that runs it. Bytecode CPython is an interpreter, but it does not read the source code line by line like a human interpreter. It works in two phases. A cook with index cards. A cook first reads through the whole recipe and writes each step on index cards in their own shorthand. If they come across an illegible sentence while doing so, they do not even start. Only when all the cards are finished do they work through them in order. A picture; what the “cards” and the “shorthand” are in CPython follows now. Bytecode is a sequence of simple instructions into which CPython translates the entire source code before it begins running it. The instructions are designed for an imaginary machine, not for a real processor. A part of CPython then works through the bytecode instruction by instruction the interpreter loop . So a Python program runs like this Figure 2 abb 2 , left ⁠ Translate. CPython reads the whole file, checks its syntax and generates bytecode from it. Nothing is run yet. ⁠ Run. The interpreter loop takes one bytecode instruction after another. For each instruction, the processor runs a piece of machine code that is part of CPython and implements exactly this instruction. For a program that you start, CPython creates the bytecode only in main memory. No executable file is produced. The picture of the human interpreter from Subsection 2.2 stufe 2 2 is therefore only half right CPython first translates the whole file and then runs it. Two ways from source code to execution. Left, Python the program python CPython translates the whole file into bytecode at every start and then works through it in its interpreter loop. Right, C the compiler translates once in advance into an executable file, which the processor then runs without the compiler. The line 1 + 2 / 1 / 2 gives rise to bytecode instructions such as “provide the number 1”, “divide”, “add”. The translator even goes one step further an expression that consists only of fixed numbers is already computed during translation. The bytecode then contains the number 1.5 directly, and there is nothing left to compute when it runs. What the bytecode looks like exactly depends on the Python version; it is an internal tool of CPython and can change with every new version. One consequence of the two phases matters in practice if any part of the file violates the syntax, no bytecode is produced at all. Then not a single line runs, not even the first. ⁠ In short CPython first translates the whole file into bytecode and then runs this bytecode instruction by instruction. Splitting up a text and checking its syntax takes a lot of work. If CPython read the text anew at every step, it would have to split up the same line a thousand times when it is run a thousand times. With bytecode, the splitting up happens once at the beginning. After that, the bytecode instructions are simple and uniform, and the interpreter loop can recognize and run each of them quickly. In addition, the bytecode is the same on all processors. Only CPython itself has to be translated once with a compiler for each processor family and each operating system; after that, it runs the same bytecode everywhere. That is why Python is said to be interpreted, even though it contains a small translator. For Python, the line between “compiled” and “interpreted” is blurred. At its core, the interpreter loop is a single loop in the C source code of CPython fetch the next bytecode instruction, look up which instruction it is, run the matching piece of machine code, start over. This is the same cycle that the processor runs through with its machine instructions fetch, decode, execute Subsection 1.2 programme und programmiersprachen.html stufe 1 2 . That is why one speaks of an imaginary or virtual machine in software, CPython plays a processor whose instructions are the bytecode. Exercises for Section 2 stufe 2 To which of the three kinds of programs does each statement apply a compiler such as gcc , an interpreter that, like a human interpreter, translates line by line and runs each line immediately, or CPython? Several answers are possible. A file is produced that runs without the translating program. The program has to be present at every start. The entire source code is translated before the first statement is run. The processor runs the translation of the source code directly. a Only the compiler it produces an executable file. CPython creates the bytecode only in main memory, and the line by line interpreter the one that works like a human interpreter produces no translation result at all. b The line by line interpreter and CPython. Both run the program themselves and therefore have to be present at every start. c The compiler and CPython. In its first phase, CPython translates the entire file into bytecode before the first line runs. Only the line by line interpreter translates each line only when it gets to it. d Only the compiler its executable file contains machine code that the processor runs directly. CPython's bytecode is run not by the processor but by the interpreter loop; meanwhile, the processor runs the machine code of CPython. On Windows, you have written two small programs that do the same thing rechner.c in C, from which you produced rechner.exe with the compiler, and rechner.py in Python. A friend uses Linux and has Python installed, but no C compiler. Can she start rechner.exe ? Explain. Can she run rechner.py ? What does she need for that? What would she have to do to use the C program? a No. rechner.exe is an executable file for Windows. It has the Windows file format and uses services of Windows; a Linux system cannot start it directly, even if the processor belongs to the same family. b Yes. She only needs a Python interpreter, which she has, in a version that knows all the language features used. She starts the program with python3 rechner.py . The source code is the same for all systems. c She needs the source code rechner.c and a C compiler for Linux, for example gcc . With it, she translates the source code anew on her computer and starts the resulting executable file. The file rechner.exe does not help her with this. A Python program has 1000 lines. Line 1000 is missing a closing parenthesis; all other lines are fine. How many lines does CPython run before it reports the error? Justify your answer with the two phases. How many lines would an interpreter run that really works like a human interpreter, that is, translates each line only when it gets to it? Which behavior would you prefer if the program overwrites a file in line 500? Why? a Not a single one. In the first phase, CPython translates the entire file. The syntax error in line 1000 prevents bytecode from being produced, and without bytecode the second phase does not begin. The message appears before line 1 runs. b 999 lines. Such an interpreter notices the error only when it gets to line 1000; it has already run everything before it. c The behavior of CPython. With a line by line interpreter, the file would already have been overwritten in line 500 when the program aborts in line 1000 a half finished state would be left behind. With CPython, a program with a syntax error does not even start running and therefore cannot leave anything half done. This does not protect against runtime errors, though they occur only during execution.
