text: To run Python programs, your computer needs CPython. This section shows how to set it up on Windows and on Linux and how to check which version you have. What you need for this opening a terminal Python is usually started with a command that you type into a terminal. A terminal is a window into which you type commands as text; the computer runs each command and writes its response below it. Opening it. ⁠ Windows 11 Right click the Start button and choose “Terminal”, or search for “Terminal” in the Start menu. A window opens with PowerShell, the command shell of Windows. ⁠ Linux Ubuntu Press Ctrl+Alt+T, or search for “Terminal” in the “Activities” overview. ⁠ Linux on Windows WSL Start the “Ubuntu” app from the Start menu. The prompt. At the end of the last line there is a short text, after which the cursor blinks. It is called the prompt and shows that the terminal is waiting for a command. On Windows, it looks something like this PS C \Users\student . On Linux, something like this student@labor ~ on Linux. You type only what comes after it. Lines without this beginning are the computer's response. Linux, Chapter 2 covers the terminal, folders and commands in detail. Python on Windows the Python install manager Windows does not come with Python. Since Python 3.14, python.org has offered its own management program for this; the earlier installer for individual versions has been deprecated since then and will no longer be released for Python 3.16. The Python install manager is a program for Windows that downloads, installs, lists, removes and starts Python versions. You operate it in the terminal with the command py . Step 1 install the install manager. It is available as the “Python install manager” app in the Microsoft Store and as a download at python.org/downloads ; both editions are the same. If you prefer to use a command, type in the terminal Step 2 install a Python version. For example, version 3.14 If no version is installed at all, the first start of py or python also fetches the newest version on its own. Step 3 check what is installed. py list shows the installed versions and which of them is the default version. py list online shows which versions are available for download. After that, py starts the default version; this is the newest installed one unless you set something else. The command python does the same. You choose a specific version with py V 3.14 . In this chapter, the command py is used on Windows. The option version makes Python state its version number without doing anything else. On the computer used to test this chapter, Python 3.13 is installed Two typical problems. ⁠ The Microsoft Store opens instead of Python. Windows creates a placeholder named python that opens the Store. In the Start menu, open “Manage app execution aliases” and check that the “Python default ” entries of the install manager are switched on. ⁠ py list reports “legacy py.exe command”. Then the old “Python Launcher” from the earlier installer is still present and takes precedence. On the computer used to test this chapter, it looks like this The old launcher does not know the command list and passes the word on to Python, which then looks for a file named list . The fix in Settings, under “Installed apps”, uninstall “Python Launcher”. A Python that was set up with the earlier installer may stay; py still finds it. ⁠ In short On Windows, you install the Python install manager and then start Python with py . On Windows, there is no fixed place where programs like Python have to be, and often several Python versions are installed side by side. In the past, every installer had to register by itself where Windows finds the command python , and several versions easily got in each other's way. A single launcher that knows all installed versions and selects the desired one solves this. Since Python 3.14, the Python install manager also takes care of installing and removing the versions. Microsoft introduced the placeholder that opens the Store in 2019 anyone who types python without Python being installed is meant to be led directly to a way of installing it. If a Python is present, the placeholder only gets in the way, as long as it stays switched on. Python on Linux Most Linux systems come with Python, because parts of the system itself are written in Python. On Linux, the command is called python3 . Checking. On Ubuntu 26.04, Python 3.14 is preinstalled The command python without the 3 does not exist there. Ubuntu responds with a hint That is why this chapter always uses python3 on Linux. If Python is missing. On very minimal systems, Python can be missing. On Ubuntu and Debian, this command installs it Here apt is the package manager of Ubuntu it downloads programs from verified sources and installs them. The sudo in front runs the command with administrator privileges and asks for your password to do so. On Linux, the system itself uses its Python. On the Ubuntu computer used to test this chapter, removing python3 would make the package manager remove more than a hundred other packages along with it, including the command helper that suggested python3 in the example above. If you remove python3 or replace it with a version you built yourself, you can damage these parts of the system. So leave the system Python as it is. If you ever need a different version, install it in addition, without touching the existing python3 . ⁠ In short On Linux, Python is usually already there and is called python3 . Python 3 appeared in 2008 and was deliberately not fully compatible with Python 2 some programs for Python 2 do not run under Python 3. At that time, many Linux systems had tools of their own written in Python 2 that were started with the command python . If python had simply been switched to Python 3, they would have broken. That is why Python 3 got its own command, python3 , and a recommendation of the Python project for Linux systems laid down that python3 always starts a Python 3. Python 2 has no longer been maintained since January 1, 2020. Since then, many systems simply leave out the command python instead of letting it point to one of the two versions. If you want it anyway, install the small package python is python3 on Ubuntu; it makes python a second name for python3 . The version number Python keeps evolving new versions bring new language features and better error messages. To know what your Python can do, you should know its version. A Python version number has the form 3.14.4 and consists of three parts the major version, here 3; the minor version, here 14; every year in October, a new minor version with new language features is released; the bugfix number, here 4; it increases when a minor version receives fixes without the language changing. Version numbers are compared part by part from the left, not as decimal numbers 3.14 is newer than 3.9 because 14 is greater than 9. The test computer for this chapter reports Python 3.13.9 on Windows and Python 3.14.4 on Linux. Both have the major version 3; the Linux version is one minor version newer. In November 2026, 3.15 is the newest minor version, 3.14 still receives bug fixes, and 3.13 receives only security fixes. All examples in this chapter run on Python 3.12 or later; they were tested on Windows with Python 3.13 and on Linux with Python 3.14. Where the output of the two versions differs, this is noted. ⁠ In short The version number tells you which Python you have; version numbers are compared part by part. Since Python 3.9 in October 2020, a new minor version has been released every year in October. Each one is maintained for about five years at first it receives bug fixes every few months, later only fixes for security vulnerabilities, and after that nothing at all. Python 3.10, for example, reached its end of life in October 2026. The fixed rhythm makes it possible to plan when you should switch to a new version. A version without maintenance keeps running, but known security vulnerabilities in it are no longer closed. Exercises for Section 3 stufe 3 Open a terminal and enter echo Hallo . Set up Python if it is missing on Windows with the Python install manager, on Linux with the package manager. Display the version number py version on Windows, python3 version on Linux. Write it down. Is it at least 3.12? Windows only What does py list show? If a warning appears, solve the problem as described in Subsection 3.2 stufe 3 2 . a The terminal responds with Hallo . b and c On the computers used to test this chapter Both versions are at least 3.12, so they are sufficient for this series. Your number may be different; all that matters is that the minor version is at least 12. d With the Python install manager, py list shows a list of the installed versions and marks the default version. If the warning about “legacy py.exe command” appears instead, the old “Python Launcher” is still installed. Uninstall it in Settings, under “Installed apps”; after that, py list responds with the list. Order the version numbers from oldest to newest 3.14.10 , 3.9.18 , 3.13.9 , 3.14.4 , 3.12.0 . Which of them meet the requirement “Python 3.12 or later”? Why is it misleading to read the numbers as decimal numbers? From oldest to newest 3.9.18 , 3.12.0 , 3.13.9 , 3.14.4 , 3.14.10 . All except 3.9.18 meet the requirement “Python 3.12 or later”. You compare part by part, starting from the left the major version is 3 everywhere; for the minor version, 9 is smaller than 12, 13 and 14; with the same minor version 14, the third number decides, and 4 is smaller than 10. Read as a decimal number, 3.9 would be larger than 3.14, because ; and 3.14.10 would look like a smaller number than 3.14.4. Both are wrong, because each part is a separate whole number and not a fractional part. In each case, explain what the cause is and what you do. On Windows, python opens the Microsoft Store, even though you have installed the Python install manager. On Ubuntu, python hallo.py responds with “Command 'python' not found”. On Windows, py list responds with a warning about “legacy py.exe command”. a The Windows placeholder that opens the Store takes precedence over the install manager's command. In the Start menu, open “Manage app execution aliases” and make sure that the “Python default ” entries of the install manager are switched on. Alternatively, use py , as in this chapter. b On Ubuntu, the command python does not exist, only python3 . The correct command is python3 hallo.py . If you absolutely want to type python , install the package python is python3 . c The old “Python Launcher” from the earlier installer is installed and hides the new command py . Uninstall it in Settings, under “Installed apps”. Until then, you can also reach the install manager under its second name pymanager , that is, with pymanager list .

title: Interactive mode
crumb: Computer Science › Programming › Python › Chapter 1: Programs and the Python Interpreter
summary: Python can be used like a calculator: you type in a line and immediately see the result.
tags: interactive mode, value, expression, evaluation, string, function, function call
ft_tags: interactive mode, value, expression, evaluation, string, function, function call
ft_text: python can be used like a calculator: you type in a line and immediately see the result. python can be used like a calculator you type in a line and immediately see the result. this section shows this way of working and the first building blocks of python values, expressions, strings and calling a function. interactive mode to try out a single line, you do not want to create a file. python offers a way of working of its own for this. a calculator. on a calculator, you type a calculation, press “=” and read off the result. then you type the next calculation. python works exactly like this when you start it without a file name. in interactive mode , python reads an input, runs it, displays the result and then waits for the next input. the prompt of the interactive mode is . this cycle of reading, running and displaying is called the read–eval–print loop , repl for short. in the terminal, start py windows or python3 linux without anything after it. python reports its version and waits for input after each , type a line and press enter. python answers on the next line and shows again. a few useful moves ⁠ exiting type exit from python 3.13 on; exit with parentheses works in every version , or press ctrl+d on linux, ctrl+z and then enter on windows. after that, the prompt of the terminal appears again. ⁠ earlier inputs the up arrow key brings back the last input; you can change it and send it again with enter. ⁠ incomplete input if something is still missing, such as a closing parenthesis, python shows ... instead of and waits for the rest of the input. from python 3.13 on, the interactive mode is in color; in this chapter, the sessions are printed without colors. ⁠ in short in interactive mode, you type a line after , and python answers immediately. the name read–eval–print loop comes from the programming language lisp. in the 1960s, lisp systems already had exactly this cycle read an input read , compute it evaluate , output the result print , start over loop . many languages have adopted it because it lets you try out a language without writing a whole program. since python 3.13, cpython has come with a revised interactive mode the prompt and the error messages are in color, you can edit multi line inputs as a whole, exit and help work without parentheses, and the keys f1, f2 and f3 open the help, the history and a mode for pasting longer texts. from python 3.14 on, it also colors the typed lines according to their syntax. in older versions and in some environments, the simpler earlier version appears; what it computes is the same. the value a calculator works with numbers. python, too, needs a name for the data it works with. a value is a single piece of data that python works with, for example the number 42 or the number 0.5. in python, numbers with decimal places are written with a point, not with a comma 0.5 , not 0,5. in this chapter, numbers in running text also use a decimal point, just as in python lines and in the answers from python. if you type in a number, the interactive mode shows its value. it writes the value the way python itself would write it and, for example, leaves out a superfluous zero at the end ⁠ in short a value is a piece of data such as the number 42; in python, decimal places come after a point. the expression usually, you do not type in a finished value but a calculation whose value python has yet to determine. an expression is a piece of source code that python can compute to a value. computing the value of an expression is called evaluation . 2 + 3 is an expression with the value 5. a single number such as 42 is also an expression, the simplest one of all its value is the number itself. the interactive mode evaluates every expression you type in and displays the value on the next line. so the sessions above are nothing but pairs of expression and value. ⁠ in short an expression is source code that yields a value; text: Python can be used like a calculator you type in a line and immediately see the result. This section shows this way of working and the first building blocks of Python values, expressions, strings and calling a function. Interactive mode To try out a single line, you do not want to create a file. Python offers a way of working of its own for this. A calculator. On a calculator, you type a calculation, press “=” and read off the result. Then you type the next calculation. Python works exactly like this when you start it without a file name. In interactive mode , Python reads an input, runs it, displays the result and then waits for the next input. The prompt of the interactive mode is . This cycle of reading, running and displaying is called the read–eval–print loop , REPL for short. In the terminal, start py Windows or python3 Linux without anything after it. Python reports its version and waits for input After each , type a line and press Enter. Python answers on the next line and shows again. A few useful moves ⁠ Exiting type exit from Python 3.13 on; exit with parentheses works in every version , or press Ctrl+D on Linux, Ctrl+Z and then Enter on Windows. After that, the prompt of the terminal appears again. ⁠ Earlier inputs The up arrow key brings back the last input; you can change it and send it again with Enter. ⁠ Incomplete input If something is still missing, such as a closing parenthesis, Python shows ... instead of and waits for the rest of the input. From Python 3.13 on, the interactive mode is in color; in this chapter, the sessions are printed without colors. ⁠ In short In interactive mode, you type a line after , and Python answers immediately. The name read–eval–print loop comes from the programming language Lisp. In the 1960s, Lisp systems already had exactly this cycle read an input read , compute it evaluate , output the result print , start over loop . Many languages have adopted it because it lets you try out a language without writing a whole program. Since Python 3.13, CPython has come with a revised interactive mode the prompt and the error messages are in color, you can edit multi line inputs as a whole, exit and help work without parentheses, and the keys F1, F2 and F3 open the help, the history and a mode for pasting longer texts. From Python 3.14 on, it also colors the typed lines according to their syntax. In older versions and in some environments, the simpler earlier version appears; what it computes is the same. The value A calculator works with numbers. Python, too, needs a name for the data it works with. A value is a single piece of data that Python works with, for example the number 42 or the number 0.5. In Python, numbers with decimal places are written with a point, not with a comma 0.5 , not 0,5. In this chapter, numbers in running text also use a decimal point, just as in Python lines and in the answers from Python. If you type in a number, the interactive mode shows its value. It writes the value the way Python itself would write it and, for example, leaves out a superfluous zero at the end ⁠ In short A value is a piece of data such as the number 42; in Python, decimal places come after a point. The expression Usually, you do not type in a finished value but a calculation whose value Python has yet to determine. An expression is a piece of source code that Python can compute to a value. Computing the value of an expression is called evaluation . 2 + 3 is an expression with the value 5. A single number such as 42 is also an expression, the simplest one of all its value is the number itself. The interactive mode evaluates every expression you type in and displays the value on the next line. So the sessions above are nothing but pairs of expression and value. ⁠ In short An expression is source code that yields a value; the interactive mode displays this value immediately. Calculating as on a calculator Python has its own symbols for the basic arithmetic operations and for powers. | Symbol | Meaning | Example | Value | | | | | | | + | plus | 7 + 2 | 9 | | | minus | 7 2 | 5 | | | times | 7 2 | 14 | | / | divided by | 7 / 2 | 3.5 | | | to the power of | 2 10 | 1024 | Rules. Python calculates as in mathematics powers before multiplication and division, multiplication and division before addition and subtraction. 100 + 220 2 gives 540; if you want to add first, you use parentheses 100 + 220 2 gives 640. Only round parentheses group a calculation. Square brackets and curly braces have other meanings in Python. Spaces around the operators are allowed but not necessary; they make a line easier to read. Python always writes the result of / with a point, even when the division comes out even 12 / 4 gives 3.0 . Powers of ten are written with e 2.5e 3 means , that is, 2.5 g if the number is a weight in kilograms. Likewise, 4.7e3 is the number 4700. Python displays results with decimal places with up to 17 significant digits. How many of them are meaningful is up to you when you read off the result. Python knows no units. You have to keep track of the unit of a number in your head. First A 450 g jar of chocolate spread costs €4.49. What does one kilogram cost? You divide the price by the weight in kilograms, that is, by 0.45. Second €1000 sits in a savings account for ten years at 2 % interest per year. The interest stays in the account and earns interest itself in the following year. So every year, the balance is multiplied by 1.02, and after ten years by in total. Third A sheet of printer paper is about 0.1 mm thick, that is , in Python 1e 4 . How high is a pack of 500 sheets? In the second line, Python first computes the power 1.02 10 and then multiplies it by 1000, powers before multiplication. Read off the kilogram costs about €9.98, after ten years there is about €1219 in the account, and the pack is 0.05 m, that is, 5 cm high. The last result. The interactive mode remembers the last displayed value under the symbol underscore , like the ANS key of a calculator. After the session above, 100 therefore gives 5.0 , the height of the pack in centimeters. This works only in interactive mode. Careful with the comma. If you are used to a decimal comma and type 2,5 2 instead of 2.5 2 out of habit, you get no error message but a wrong result Python reads the comma as a separator between two values 2 and 5 2 . It displays both in parentheses instead of computing 5.0. ⁠ In short Python calculates with + / and round parentheses according to the rules of mathematics; decimal places come after a point, and it knows no units. For “to the power of”, no single symbol has become established in programming languages. Python follows the notation , which the language Fortran already used in the 1950s. The symbol ^ , on the other hand, Python took over from the language C, where it means an operation on individual binary digits that has nothing to do with powers. That is why 2 ^ 3 gives 1 in Python and not 8, and it does so without an error message. If you are used to the symbol ^ from spreadsheets or calculators, watch out for this. The recipe in interactive mode first by hand, then ready made With what has been explained so far, you can run Heron's recipe from Subsection 1.1 programme und programmiersprachen.html stufe 1 1 in interactive mode first by hand, pass by pass, then with the ready made way that comes with Python. By hand. The first pass with is 1 + 2/1 / 2 . For every further pass, you need the last result as the new ; stands for it. With the up arrow key, you bring back the line + 2/ / 2 and send it again After the fifth pass, nothing changes anymore the recipe has reached its goal. Ready made. The square root is the power with the exponent . Python can therefore compute it without a recipe Comparison. Both ways agree in the first 15 decimal places | Way | Result | | | | | Heron by hand, from the 5th pass on | 1.414213562373095 | | ready made with 2 0.5 | 1.4142135623730951 | | true value | | The difference in the 16th decimal place has a simple cause Python does not calculate with infinitely many digits but rounds every intermediate result to a fixed number of digits. Between two neighboring rounded numbers, there is therefore a smallest step. The recipe rounds several times in each pass and in the end stays one such step away from the built in result. Here the ready made way lies closer to the true value and needs no passes and no starting estimate; that is why you use it whenever it exists. By hand, every pass had to be sent off individually. Taking exactly such repetitions off your hands is what a program is for. ⁠ In short Heron's recipe runs in interactive mode pass by pass and, after five passes, arrives at the built in result of 2 0.5 except for the last digit. Text as a value the string Programs output not only numbers but also text, such as “Price in euros ” before a result. Text must therefore be able to be a value, too. A string is a value that consists of text. In source code, it stands between two straight quotation marks, "Hallo" , or between two apostrophes, 'Hallo' . Three inputs in interactive mode The interactive mode displays a string with apostrophes, even if you typed it with quotation marks; both mean the same. The second line is more important "7 6" is not computed. Between quotation marks, 7 6 is just a sequence of five characters. The quotation marks must be the straight ones from the keyboard. The typographic curly quotes from a word processor, “ and ” in English or „ and “ in German, are different characters for Python. ⁠ In short Text in straight quotation marks is a string, that is, a value that Python does not calculate with. The interactive mode displays every value the way you would write it in source code. That is why '7 6' appears there with apostrophes and 42 without you can see at once whether the result is a number or a text. Without this marking, the number 42 and the text made of the characters “4” and “2” could not be told apart on the screen. The function Many tasks occur in almost every program, for example writing something on the screen. For these, Python comes with ready made subprograms. A key on the calculator. The key of a calculator triggers a small built in program. You do not need to know how it calculates; you put a number in and get the square root out. A function is a ready made subprogram with a name that you can have run when needed. Python comes with the function named print . It writes values as text to the terminal. ⁠ In short A function is a ready made subprogram with a name. The function call print A function does something only when you have it run. There is a fixed notation for this. A function call has a function run. You write its name, followed by round parentheses, and inside the parentheses the values that the function is to work with, separated by commas. The function print writes the values in its parentheses on one line, separated by one space each. Strings appear without quotation marks. If there is an expression in the parentheses, Python evaluates it first and then outputs its value. A call without values, print , writes an empty line. In interactive mode, "Hallo" and print "Hallo" look similar but are different. In the first case, the interactive mode displays the value of an expression, with apostrophes. In the second case, the function print itself writes the text to the terminal, without apostrophes. Afterwards, the call of print has no value that the interactive mode would still display. ⁠ In short You call a function with its name and round parentheses; print writes the values in the parentheses to the terminal. Exercises for Section 4 stufe 4 Calculate in interactive mode and give the results with a sensible number of digits and with a unit. A car needs 45 liters of gasoline for 750 km. How many liters does it need for one kilometer? A square room with a side length of 4.5 m is to be tiled. A tile of 60 cm by 60 cm covers . What is the minimum number of tiles you need? Compute the area with . A hair on your head grows about 0.35 mm per day. How much does it grow in a year of 365 days? Calculate in meters and write the 0.35 mm with e for this. Directly after a , continue calculating with and give the consumption in liters per 100 kilometers. a Liters divided by kilometers liters per kilometer. b The area of the room is , and . Python computes the power first, so parentheses are not needed. You cannot buy partial tiles you need at least 57 tiles, and the ones at the edge are cut to size. c , in Python 3.5e 4 . In one year, that makes , or just under 13 cm. d Directly after a , holds the value 0.06 ; 100 gives 6.0 , that is, 6 liters per 100 kilometers. If you calculate b or c first, holds their result, because always holds only the most recently displayed value. Run Heron's recipe for in interactive mode start with 1 + 3/1 / 2 and repeat + 3/ / 2 until the result no longer changes. How many passes do you need? Compute the ready made way and compare. For , the two ways differed in the last digit. What about here? a After five passes, the result no longer changes; the sixth only confirms this. b 3 0.5 gives 1.7320508075688772 . c This time, the two ways agree down to the last digit. Whether the recipe lands exactly on the built in result or one smallest step next to it depends on how the individual roundings turn out; for it stayed just off, for it hits. In both cases, the ready made way is the more reliable one. For each input, write down what the interactive mode displays. Then check on the computer. 12 / 3 "12 / 3" print 12 / 3 print "12 / 3 =", 12 / 3 2,5 + 1 2 3 2 a The result of / is always written with a point, even when the division comes out even. b Nothing is calculated between quotation marks; the interactive mode shows the string with apostrophes. c print first evaluates the expression and then writes the value. d print writes the string without quotation marks, then a space, and then the value. e The comma separates two values, 2 and 5 + 1 . Python, however, does not recognize typographic quotation marks as the beginning or end of a string. A word processor is therefore unsuitable for programs. An editor is a program with which you write and save plain text files. An editor for programmers also helps you write source code it colors the code according to its syntax, marks violations of the syntax while you type and can run a program at the push of a button. ⁠ Visual Studio Code VS Code for short is a free editor for Windows and Linux, which you can get at code.visualstudio.com . On Ubuntu, you can alternatively install it with sudo snap install classic code . After the first start, install the “Python” extension from Microsoft via the Extensions icon on the left edge. It provides the coloring, the error marking and the button for running a program; it does not contain Python itself. ⁠ IDLE is a simple editor that is part of Python. On Windows, the Python install manager creates the entry “IDLE Python 3.14 ” in the Start menu, matching the installed version. On Ubuntu, you install it with sudo apt install idle and start it with the command idle . You begin a new program with “File”, “New File”. For the programs in this chapter, create a folder python kurs in your home folder and save all files there. In VS Code, you open this folder with “File”, “Open Folder”; you then create new files in it. On Windows, File Explorer often hides file name extensions. Turn them on “View”, “Show”, “File name extensions” so that you can see whether a file is really called hallo.py and not hallo.py.txt . ⁠ In short You write programs with an editor that saves plain text, ideally with an editor for programmers such as VS Code or IDLE. While you type, an editor for programmers constantly reads the source code along and splits it up the same way the translator of CPython does in its first phase Subsection 2.4 vom quelltext zur ausfuhrung compiler und interpreter.html stufe 2 4 into numbers, operators, parentheses, strings and names. Each kind of component gets its own color; a string that is never closed therefore visibly colors the rest of the line as well. Then the editor checks the components against the grammar of the language and underlines every place where the grammar is violated. This check is the same kind of check that CPython performs before running a program; the editor merely does it earlier, namely while you are writing. What will happen when the program runs, on the other hand, it cannot fully foresee. The script With an editor, you can write the source code of a program into a file and run it as often as you like. A script is a text file with Python source code whose name ends in .py . Python runs a script by translating the file and then running each of its lines once, from top to bottom. Preparing the folder. Two commands are enough, and they are the same on Windows and Linux mkdir python kurs creates the folder python kurs , and cd python kurs changes into it in the terminal. A newly opened terminal is in your home folder; that is where the folder is created. If you have already created it in the editor, you can skip mkdir . In detail Linux, Chapter 2. In the editor, write these three lines and save them as hallo.py in the folder python kurs In the terminal, you change into the folder and start the script by writing the file name after py or python3 Python translates the file, runs the three lines in order and ends; after that, the prompt of the terminal appears again. The second line outputs the value of 2 + 3 , the third outputs the string "2 + 3" literally. In VS Code, the button with the triangle at the top right “Run Python File” runs the same command in the terminal at the bottom of the window. In a script, only print displays anything. This script shows the most important difference from interactive mode The line 2 + 3 is run, but its value appears nowhere. In interactive mode, the same line would have displayed 5 . In a script, only what a call of print outputs appears. Figure 3 abb 3 shows both ways of working side by side. On Windows, the output looks exactly the same. Two ways of working. Left, the interactive mode it reads an input, evaluates it, displays the value and starts over. Right, a script Python translates the whole file and then runs the lines one after another; only what print outputs becomes visible. ⁠ In short A script is a .py file that you run with py datei.py or python3 datei.py ; only what print outputs becomes visible in it. The rule is stated this way in the Python Language Reference if a line is just an expression, its value is displayed in interactive mode; in a script, it is computed and discarded. Technically, the interactive mode translates each input in a separate mode of operation that appends an instruction “display value” at the end; when a script is translated, this instruction is missing. With 2 + 3 , the translator goes even further it computes the line in advance, recognizes that its value is not needed anywhere and leaves it out of the bytecode entirely. The reason for the rule is practical. A program should output exactly what its author wants. If a script with a hundred lines of calculation displayed every intermediate result, the actual result would get lost among them. When trying things out in interactive mode, on the other hand, you want to see every value immediately. The comment A script is read more often than it is written, and after a few weeks, even you no longer know what 500 / 4 6 was supposed to mean. You need room for explanations that do not disturb Python. A comment begins with the character and extends to the end of the line. Python skips it completely. A recipe for pizza dough serves 4 people and needs 500 g of flour and 300 ml of water. For 6 people, you divide each amount by 4, which gives the amount for one person, and multiply it by 6 On Windows py rezept.py , the same output appears. The first three lines are entirely comments. In the last two, the comment comes after the statement Python runs the call of print and skips the rest of the line from on. Good comments say what a number means and why something is calculated, not what is written there anyway. In the example, they state the assumptions and the units, because Python does not know those. With a at the beginning of a line, you can also switch off a line temporarily without deleting it. ⁠ In short A comment begins with , applies up to the end of the line and is there only for humans. During translation, CPython first splits the source code up into its smallest components numbers, names, operators, parentheses, strings. A comment is thrown away in this very first step. It no longer appears in the bytecode, and therefore it costs no time when the program runs, however long it is. A inside a string does not start a comment, because there it belongs to the text print "Nr. 5" outputs Nr. 5 . Exercises for Section 5 stufe 5 Using an editor, write the script hallo.py from Subsection 5.2 stufe 5 2 and add 7 6 as a fourth line. Write down what the script will output before you start it. Start it in the terminal and compare. Change the fourth line so that its value appears as well. a and b The script outputs three lines; the fourth line, 7 6 , is computed, but its value does not appear, because in a script only print displays anything On Windows py hallo.py , the output is the same. c The fourth line must read print 7 6 ; then 42 appears as well. Following the model of rezept.py , write a script rezept10.py that converts the pizza dough for 10 people. Besides 500 g of flour and 300 ml of water, the recipe for 4 people contains 10 g of salt. The script should output all three amounts with their units. Comment the assumptions and the calculation. As a check, redo the calculation in your head. Check in your head for one person, it is 125 g of flour, 75 ml of water and 2.5 g of salt, so for ten people ten times as much. The 1250 g of flour are a little more than a standard 1 kg bag. On Windows, the output is the same. A liter of gasoline costs €1.80. For the car from Exercise 10 der interaktive modus.html aufg 10 , which needs 45 liters for 750 km, someone calculated in interactive mode Write a script verbrauch.py that outputs the same three results with explanatory text, such as Liter pro km 0.06 . Why can you not use here? Replace it with an expression that does without . On Windows, the output is the same. Only the interactive mode keeps track of ; in a script there is no “most recently displayed result”, because a script does not display values at all. If you nevertheless write print "Liter pro 100 km ", 100 in a script, it aborts with NameError name ' ' is not defined . That is why the second line contains the whole expression 45 / 750 100 .

text: Everyone who programs makes mistakes. This section distinguishes three kinds of errors and shows when Python notices them and how to read its error messages. The syntax error The first kind of error concerns the form of the source code. An illegible recipe. A cook who comes across an illegible sentence while reading through a recipe does not even start cooking. First, they report which sentence cannot be read. A syntax error is a place in the source code that violates the syntax of the language. Python reports it before any line of the file is run. This follows from the two phases from Subsection 2.4 vom quelltext zur ausfuhrung compiler und interpreter.html stufe 2 4 first the whole file is translated, and with a syntax error, no bytecode is produced that could run. The closing parenthesis is missing in the third line Although the first two lines are free of errors, not even “Zeile 1” German for “line 1” appears. The message consists of four lines the file and line number, the affected line, a ^ character below the place where Python pins down the error, and finally the error type SyntaxError with a description, here that the parenthesis was never closed. Further common syntax errors and their messages | Line | Message and cause | | | | | print "Ende | unterminated string literal The string is never closed. | | print "Hallo" | unmatched ' ' A parenthesis is closed that was never opened. | | print „Hallo“ | invalid character '„' U+201E a typographic instead of a straight quotation mark. | | a line that begins with spaces | IndentationError unexpected indent Spaces at the beginning of a line have a meaning in Python and must not stand there without a reason. | In interactive mode, a syntax error affects only that one input; after that, appears again. ⁠ In short A syntax error violates the form; Python reports it before the start, and no line of the file runs. The syntax of Python allows only the straight quotation mark " and the apostrophe ' as the beginning and end of a string. The curly quotes that a word processor inserts while you type, “ and ” in English or „ and “ in German, are completely different characters for Python. They are allowed inside a string; outside of one, they do not belong to any component of the language. Python therefore rejects a file with the line print „Hallo“ as early as during translation The message names the forbidden character together with its number every written character has a number that is fixed worldwide, and U+201E is the number of the low quotation mark that opens a quotation in German. On the screen, the characters „ and " look similar; the number tells them apart unambiguously. The runtime error Source code can be completely correct in its form and still demand something that cannot be carried out. A missing ingredient. The cook has read the recipe and begins. At step 2, they discover that the eggs are missing. By then, they have already done step 1; they get no further than step 2. A runtime error is an error that occurs only when a line is run. All lines before it have already run; the program aborts at this point. Division by zero is allowed in its form but cannot be carried out This time, “Zeile 1” appears the file was translated without errors, and the first line has run. In the second line, the division fails, the program aborts, and “Zeile 3” never appears. Figure 4 abb 4 contrasts the two cases. Syntax error and runtime error. On the left, an error of form in line 3 prevents even the translation; no line runs. On the right, the translation succeeds, line 1 runs, and the error occurs only when line 2 is run. ⁠ In short A runtime error occurs when a line is run; everything before it has run, nothing after it has. The reason is the two phases of CPython Subsection 2.4 vom quelltext zur ausfuhrung compiler und interpreter.html stufe 2 4 . In the first phase, the translator checks only the form, and it does so for the whole file. Without a valid form, no bytecode is produced, and the second phase does not even begin. Whether a line can actually be run only becomes apparent in the second phase, when the interpreter loop reaches it. This is remarkable in the case of 5 / 0 . The translator does compute fixed numeric expressions such as 2 + 3 in advance Subsection 2.4 vom quelltext zur ausfuhrung compiler und interpreter.html stufe 2 4 , but not the division by zero it deliberately leaves it in the bytecode. Its meaning is defined as “an error occurs when this line is run”. If the translator computed it in advance and failed in doing so, line 1 would not run either, and the program would behave differently from what the semantics prescribes. The exception Python needs a uniform way to report an error and to stop the program at that point. An exception is the event with which Python reports an error. It has a type, for example ZeroDivisionError , and a description, for example division by zero . If it occurs while the program is running, it aborts the program at that point. So a runtime error raises an exception. Python also reports a syntax error as an exception, with the type SyntaxError , only already during translation. Three types of exceptions that occur in this chapter SyntaxError The source code violates the syntax. ZeroDivisionError A division by zero. NameError Python does not know a name. This typically happens when the quotation marks around a text are missing. Without quotation marks, Python takes a word to be a name, as print is one, and looks for something with that name The description sometimes depends on the version. If you divide a number with decimal places by zero, Python 3.13 on Windows reports ZeroDivisionError float division by zero , while Python 3.14 on Linux reports only ZeroDivisionError division by zero . The type stays the same. ⁠ In short An exception reports an error with a type and a description; while the program is running, it aborts the program. The traceback When an exception aborts a program, you want to know what happened, where and why. Python provides a report with a fixed structure for this. The traceback is the report that Python outputs when an exception aborts a program while it is running. It names the place in the source code where the exception occurred and, in its last line, the type and the description of the exception. Figure 5 abb 5 breaks the traceback of laufzeitfehler.py down into its parts. A traceback broken down into its parts Linux; on Windows, line 2 contains the Windows path . You read it from the bottom first the exception 5 , then the location 2 to 4 . You read a traceback from the bottom the last line says what happened, the lines above it say where. In longer programs, there are further location lines above the error location, because the traceback traces the whole path to the error location; the lowest location line is always the place where the exception actually occurred. The marker below the line has existed since Python 3.11. If the error concerns the whole line, Python leaves the marker out. In interactive mode, instead of a file name, there is , counted from the first input; in the simpler earlier version of the interactive mode, it says After the traceback, the interactive mode simply waits for the next input. ⁠ In short A traceback names the location and the type of an exception; you read it from the bottom. The header already says it most recent call last , the most recent step comes last. A traceback is in chronological order. It begins where the program started and ends where it failed. In the programs in this chapter, this path is only one step long. Larger programs consist of parts that call each other; then the traceback lists every part on the way to the error location, and the list becomes long. For finding the error, however, the end of the path is almost always what matters first. That is why you read from the bottom. A practical side effect in the terminal, the output scrolls away upward, and the last lines remain visible. With a long traceback, the most important part is therefore exactly where your eye looks after the program has ended. The logic error Python does not report the most dangerous kind of error at all. The wrong recipe. A cook follows a recipe that says “salt” instead of “sugar”. Every step is readable and can be carried out; the cake even turns out fine, it just does not taste good. A logic error is an error in which a program runs without an error message but does not compute what was intended. If you drive a route at 60 km/h there and at 40 km/h back, your average speed is not 50 km/h but lower on the way back, you are on the road longer, so the slow speed counts for longer. If each direction is 120 km long, the way there takes 2 hours and the way back 3. For 240 km, you then need 5 hours, so on average km/h. In general, the average speed is , where is the speed on the way there and the speed on the way back. Here this gives . In the following script, the parentheses around the denominator are missing Following its rules, Python calculates and is right to do so; something else was intended. The average must lie between the two speeds, that is, between 40 and 60 km/h; 120 km/h cannot be right. With 2 60 40 / 60 + 40 , the result is 48.0 . Further typical logic errors from this chapter a comma instead of a point 2,5 2 gives two values instead of 5.0 Subsection 4.4 der interaktive modus.html stufe 4 4 ; ^ instead of 2 ^ 3 gives 1 instead of 8; a wrong unit a price in euros is labeled “cents”. What helps against it. Check every result with a case whose answer you know, or with a rough estimate. For the average, two equal speeds are suitable if you drive at 50 km/h there and back, your average speed is 50 km/h. The correct formula gives 50, the wrong one 150. ⁠ In short A logic error runs without a message and yields a wrong result; you find it only by checking results. Python checks the form during translation and, while the program runs, whether each line can be run. What the author meant is written nowhere in the source code, so Python cannot check it either. Behind this lies a fundamental limit. Computer science has proven that there can be no method that decides, for every arbitrary program, whether its behavior has a particular property that some programs have and others do not, such as “always outputs the correct average speed”. This is Rice's theorem from 1953. Tools can find many typical errors, but never all of them. Comparing results with known cases therefore remains indispensable. Which lines of the script have run? How can you tell? What did the author probably mean, and what is the correct line if the distance is to be output in meters? a A NameError in line 4 line 4 in the location line, the type in the last line . b Lines 1 to 3. Line 1 is a comment and does nothing; the output of lines 2 and 3 appears before the traceback. Line 4 is where the error occurred; it has output nothing, because Python wanted to evaluate the expression Strecke 1000 before calling print . c The author probably meant the distance from line 3, 45 km. But the name Strecke does not occur anywhere; Python does not know it. The correct fix is to write out the expression itself, with 2.5 hours for 2 h 30 min print "Strecke in m ", 18 2.5 1000 . Then Strecke in m 45000.0 appears. For each of the three scripts, write down what it outputs, and assign the error to one of the three kinds. Then check on the computer. For fehler b.py , pay close attention to whether “Liter pro km ” still appears. ⁠ fehler a.py has a syntax error in line 3, the string is never closed. Therefore no line runs; not even “Start” appears ⁠ fehler b.py has a runtime error line 1 runs, line 2 aborts. “Liter pro km ” does not appear, because Python first evaluates all values in the parentheses, including 45 / 0 , and only after that would print write anything. The marker points to the division ⁠ fehler c.py runs through without a message but contains a logic error 45 / 750 is the consumption for one kilometer, but it is labeled as the consumption for 100 kilometers. The correct line would be print "Liter pro 100 km ", 45 / 750 100 with the output 6.0 , or the label “Liter pro km ”. On Windows, all three outputs are the same; only the location lines name the Windows path. Anna and Ben buy a lottery ticket together. Anna pays €1, Ben €2. The ticket wins €12, and the prize is divided in proportion to the stakes Ben's share is the prize times Ben's stake divided by the sum of both stakes. The script outputs Bens Anteil in Euro 26.0 . How can you tell without calculating that this cannot be right? Find the error and correct the line. Check the corrected formula with a case whose result you know. a A share can never be larger than the whole prize, here €12. €26 for Ben is therefore impossible. b The denominator lacks parentheses. Python computes . Correct Output Bens Anteil in Euro 8.0 . Ben gets €8, Anna the remaining €4; that fits, because Ben paid in twice as much. c With equal stakes, each must get exactly half 12 1 / 1 + 1 gives 6.0 . A second known case if Ben pays much more than Anna, he gets almost the whole prize; if he pays nothing, he gets nothing. Python comes with a tool that displays the bytecode of a file without running it. You call it in the terminal with py m dis or python3 m dis , followed by the file name. For this, save this script Have the bytecode displayed python3 m dis rechnung.py Linux or py m dis rechnung.py Windows . Each group of instructions begins with the number of the source code line it comes from. Can you find the comment again? Look for the instructions for line 2. Is there still an addition, or already the number 5? Look for the instructions for line 3. Has 5 / 0 been computed in advance? Use the Background box in Subsection 6.2 stufe 6 2 to explain why. Then run the script. What appears before the traceback comes? The names of the instructions depend on the Python version; the observations do not. The output on the two test computers a There are no instructions for line 1; the comment disappeared during translation. The first group after the start instruction RESUME begins with the line number 2. b In line 2, there is no addition. The translator has already computed 2 + 3 Python 3.13 loads the finished number with LOAD CONST 0 5 , Python 3.14 with LOAD SMALL INT 5 . After that comes the call of print CALL . c In line 3, 5 and 0 are loaded individually, followed by BINARY OP 11 / the division takes place only during execution. The translator computes in advance only what succeeds. If it computed 5 / 0 already during translation, the error would occur before line 2 runs. The semantics, however, require that the error occur exactly when line 3 is run, after everything before it has run. d First, 5 from line 2 appears, then the traceback with ZeroDivisionError in line 3 The fact that the instruction names of the two versions differ LOAD CONST versus LOAD SMALL INT , RETURN CONST versus LOAD CONST and RETURN VALUE shows that the bytecode is an internal tool of CPython that may change with every version.

text: Everything Python calculates with lies in main memory as an object. This section clarifies what an object is, how Python recognizes what you are allowed to do with an object and how you tell two objects apart. The object Chapter 1 /wissen/en/informatik/programmieren/python/programme und der python interpreter/programme und der python interpreter.html called numbers such as 42 and texts such as "Hallo" values Chapter 1, Section 4.2 /wissen/en/informatik/programmieren/python/programme und der python interpreter/der interaktive modus.html stufe 4 2 . While Python works with a value, this value has to be stored somewhere. And Python has to know what kind of value it is you can calculate with the number 42, but not with the text made of the characters 4 and 2. A labeled box. You can picture main memory as a long row of compartments. Python puts each value into a box of its own. On the box, it writes what kind of value lies inside, and each box stands at a fixed place with a place number Fig. 1 abb 1 . This is a picture for orientation how memory is built technically does not matter for what follows. Three objects in main memory, drawn as boxes. Each box carries a label saying what kind of value it contains, and it stands at a fixed place. On the screen, the first and the third number look the same; for Python, they are different things. The place numbers are made up. An object is a piece of main memory in which Python stores a value, together with the information about what kind of value is stored there. Every value Python works with is contained in an object every number, every string, even every intermediate result of a calculation. If you type 42 , 4.0 and "42" one after the other in interactive mode, Python calculates with three objects as in Fig. 1 abb 1 The first contains the integer 42, the second a number with decimal places, the third the text made of the characters 4 and 2. The interactive mode already shows the kind in the notation without a point, with a point, with apostrophes. ⁠ In short An object is a value in main memory that carries the information about its kind with it. The type Before Python combines two values, it has to know what is allowed with them. The plus sign means something different for two numbers than for two texts, and for a number and a text it means nothing at all. The label on the box. In Fig. 1 abb 1 , each box says what kind of value it contains. In Python, this label has a name of its own. The type of an object is the kind of its value. It determines which values the object can have and what you can do with it. The function type returns the type of an object. The three objects from Fig. 1 abb 1 have three different types is Python's way of writing “the type int ”; the word class stands for a type here. The three names are abbreviations | Type | short for | meaning | examples | | | | | | | int | integer | whole number | 42 , 7 , 0 | | float | floating point number | number with decimal places | 4.0 , 0.5 , 2.5e 3 | | str | string | sequence of characters | "42" , 'Regen' | Which type a number gets is decided by its notation alone without a point and without e , it is an int ; with a point or with e , it is a float . That is why 4e3 is also a float , although the value 4000 is a whole number The plus sign shows what the type does. For two objects of type int , it adds; for two objects of type str , it joins the texts together; and for a str and an int , Python knows no rule The exception Chapter 1, Section 6.3 /wissen/en/informatik/programmieren/python/programme und der python interpreter/fehler lesen und verstehen.html stufe 6 3 is of type TypeError . The description gives the reason a str can only be extended by another str , not by an int . So Python does not convert the number 3 into the text "3" on its own. ⁠ In short The type says what kind of value an object contains and what you can do with it; type displays it. Main memory holds nothing but patterns of numbers. The same pattern can mean a number or a sequence of letters, depending on how you read it. That is why, in CPython, every object carries a reference to its type, right at the beginning of its memory area. When the interpreter loop Chapter 1, Section 2.4 /wissen/en/informatik/programmieren/python/programme und der python interpreter/vom quelltext zur ausfuhrung compiler und interpreter.html stufe 2 4 encounters a plus sign, it looks up the type of both values and carries out the addition rule that belongs to these types. If there is no matching rule, it raises a TypeError . In the C language, this is different there, you write down in the source code which type each memory cell has, and the compiler already chooses the matching machine instruction during translation. In the finished program, the type no longer appears anywhere. This makes C faster, because nothing has to be looked up. Python pays for the lookup with time on every calculation and gains flexibility in return the same line of source code can work once with integers, once with floating point numbers and once with text. The identity Two objects can have the same type and the same value and still be two different boxes. To tell them apart, each object needs a mark that only it has. The place number. In Fig. 1 abb 1 , each box stands at a place of its own. You recognize two boxes with the same label and the same content by their different place numbers. The identity of an object is an integer that distinguishes the object from all other objects that exist at the same time. It does not change as long as the object exists. The function id returns it. The identity is a long number that looks random On your computer, other numbers appear, and different ones again the next time Python starts. That does not matter the numerical value never matters, only whether two objects have the same identity. For numbers and strings, moreover, the value of an object stays the same forever. A calculation does not change any existing object. It returns a new object that contains the result 2 + 3 leaves the objects 2 and 3 untouched and returns an object with the value 5. ⁠ In short The identity is the fixed number of an object; id displays it. In CPython, the identity is the address at which the object begins in main memory. Hence the large numbers. Other programs that run Python may assign other numbers; the language only requires that the number is unique and does not change. Unique means unique among the objects that exist at the same time. CPython frees an object that no part of the program needs anymore, and its place can be used for a new object. Two objects that exist one after the other can therefore get the same number. So if you compare identities, you have to make sure that both objects still exist. The method Some abilities of a type do not fit any arithmetic symbol converting a text to capital letters or writing a number as a fraction. For this, every type comes with functions of its own. Functions that belong to the box. A function is a ready made subprogram with a name Chapter 1, Section 4.7 /wissen/en/informatik/programmieren/python/programme und der python interpreter/der interaktive modus.html stufe 4 7 . Some functions are attached to a type like buttons on a device you press them on a particular object, and they work with exactly this object. A method is a function that belongs to a type. You call it for an object by writing a dot, the name of the method and parentheses after the object. The type str has a method upper that returns the text in capital letters. The type float has a method as integer ratio that writes the number as a fraction of numerator and denominator The answer 5, 2 consists of two values in parentheses the numerator 5 and the denominator 2, because . The last input shows that each method belongs to its type a float has no method upper . Python reports this as an AttributeError nothing named upper is attached to the object. The parentheses around 2.5 ensure that Python does not take the dot before the method name for a decimal point. For an integer, you need them without parentheses, Python would read 19. as the beginning of the number . ⁠ In short A method is a function of a type; you call it with objekt.name . Why is the value alone not enough for this, and why are value and type together not enough either? The picture shows two boxes with the label float and the content at two different places. Python tells them apart by their identity, the place number that id displays. The value alone is not enough, because both have the same value; value and type together are not enough either, because the types are the same, too. Only the identity is different for each object, as long as both exist at the same time. Whether two such objects exist separately at all or whether Python uses a single one is up to Python itself; but the question of how they differ arises as soon as there are two.

text: Integers are Python's simplest number type. This section shows how large they can become, which arithmetic operators Python knows and how it divides with a whole number result, also with negative numbers. The type int Item counts, scores, page numbers, account numbers many things in everyday life are whole numbers. There, you want to calculate exactly, without any rounding, even when the numbers become very large. Digits, as many as needed. On paper, you write an integer with as many digits as it needs. A three digit number needs three digits, a thirty digit number thirty. Python handles integers in exactly this way. The type int comprises the integers An object of type int has no fixed size it grows as large as the number requires and is limited only by main memory. Adding, subtracting and multiplying two int values always yields the exact result as an int . You write an int as a sequence of digits without a point, negative numbers with a minus sign in front. Long numbers may be structured with underscores 1 000 000 is the same number as 1000000 . has 31 digits and is computed exactly. Even a calculation in which a small number stands between two huge ones loses nothing ⁠ In short An int is an integer of arbitrary size; Python calculates with it exactly. A processor calculates with integers of a fixed size. A common size reaches up to ; the machine instruction cuts off anything beyond that, and the result is wrong. The integer types of the C language have such fixed limits. That is why CPython does not store an int as a single machine number but like a number on paper as a sequence of digits. Only the base is not 10 but . Each “digit” is a number from 0 to and occupies a memory word of its own; the sign is stored separately in front. When a number grows, CPython appends further digits. The arithmetic works like the written arithmetic you learned at school digit by digit with carries, each step with ordinary machine instructions. The price is time an addition of large numbers needs many machine instructions instead of a single one. Python can calculate with arbitrarily large int values. For display, however, it has to convert the number into decimal digits, and for huge numbers this is much more costly than any addition the effort grows considerably faster than the number of digits. An attacker could send a server that reads numbers from texts a number with millions of digits and thus keep it busy for a long time. Since Python 3.11, Python therefore refuses conversions with more than 4300 decimal digits. The vulnerability is publicly described under the identifier CVE 2020 10735. The number has been computed; only the display fails. The message names the way to shift the limit. Conversions into systems with a power of two as the base are exempt, because they are fast. Python knows further such symbols, and there is a general name for them. A small machine. An arithmetic symbol takes in values and puts out a new value, like a small machine with inputs and one output. An operator is a symbol that computes a new value from values. The values an operator acts on are called its operands . An operator with two operands is called binary, one with only one operand unary. In 7 2 , the minus is binary; in 7 , it is unary it turns 7 into the number . Python has seven arithmetic operators | Operator | Meaning | Example | | | | | | + | addition | 7 + 2 gives 9 | | | subtraction; unary sign | 7 2 gives 5 | | | multiplication | 7 2 gives 14 | | / | division | 7 / 2 gives 3.5 | | // | floor division | 7 // 2 gives 3 | | % | remainder | 7 % 2 gives 1 | | | power | 7 2 gives 49 | Which type the result has. If both operands are an int , the result is also an int , with one exception division / always returns a float . If at least one operand is a float , Python turns the other one into a float as well, and the result is a float ⁠ In short An operator computes a new value from its operands; if one operand is a float , so is the result. Division Price divided by weight, distance divided by time you need ordinary division all the time, and it should return the result you know from mathematics. The operator / divides the left operand by the right one. The result is always a float , even if both operands are an int and the division leaves no remainder. This explains the observation from Chapter 1 /wissen/en/informatik/programmieren/python/programme und der python interpreter/programme und der python interpreter.html that 12 / 4 gives the answer 3.0 Dividing by zero is not possible; Python reports a ZeroDivisionError . If you divide a float by zero, the description in Python 3.13 is float division by zero ; from Python 3.14 on, it is division by zero , as with integers. ⁠ In short / divides as in mathematics and always returns a float . In the old versions 2.x of the Python language, 7 / 2 gave the integer 3, as in C two integers were divided with a whole number result, floating point numbers in the ordinary way. The result thus depended on which type the values happened to have, and not on what the programmer meant. A calculation such as “sum of the grades divided by their count” gave the value 4.5 for the grades 4.0 and 5.0 , but silently gave the value 4 for the same grades written as 4 and 5 . Because nowhere in Python do you fix which type a value must have, integers easily slipped into such calculations. With Python 3.0 2008 , the two meanings were therefore separated / always divides as in mathematics, and if you want a whole number division, you write a separate operator for it. Since then, an expression means the same thing regardless of whether integers or floating point numbers go into it. Floor division and remainder 125 minutes are 2 hours and 5 minutes. For such calculations, you need two numbers how many times 60 fits completely into 125, and what is left over. Multiples on the number line. Mark all multiples of the divisor on the number line, for example all multiples of 2. Every integer then lies either on a multiple or between two of them. The nearest multiple to the left of or itself is ; the distance from there to is the remainder Fig. 2 abb 2 . For , the multiple is and the remainder is 1. For , the nearest multiple to the left is , not , and the remainder is again 1. Floor division by 2 on the number line. Each number has a nearest multiple of 2 to its left, ; the distance to is the remainder. For , ; for , . In both cases, the remainder is 1. For integers and , a // b is the largest integer that is not greater than . This is the quotient rounded down, that is, toward . The remainder is a % b . The operator // is called floor division ; the operator % returns the remainder . Two rules follow from the definition that are worth remembering. For all integers and , For , the remainder lies in the range ; for , in the range . So the remainder always has the sign of or is zero. 2.1 gl 2 1 is the definition of the remainder, solved for . Both operators also work with floating point numbers ⁠ In short // rounds the quotient down, toward ; % is the matching remainder and has the sign of the right operand. In C, integer division rounds toward zero there, , and for Equation 2.1 gl 2 1 to hold, the remainder must be . Python rounds down because then, for , the remainder always lies between 0 and , whatever the sign of . This is exactly the property you need for everything that repeats periodically ⁠ Time of day If a clock counts seconds since a reference time, t % 86400 is the second of the day, even for times before the reference time, that is, for negative . One second before midnight is 1 % 86400 , which gives 86399, that is, 23 59 59. ⁠ Angles A rotation by ends in the same direction as a rotation by . 90 % 360 gives 270; every angle lands in the range from to below . Once you have decided on this remainder, the quotient is fixed by 2.1 gl 2 1 , , and that is the rounded down quotient. The same choice is common in number theory. That C calculates differently probably has historical reasons the arithmetic units of the processors of the time divided toward zero, and since 1999 the C language standard has strictly prescribed this rounding. The power Powers of ten for very large and very small numbers, powers of two for memory sizes, squares for areas, compound interest powers occur in many calculations. Both rules come from mathematical notation. There, means ; if you mean , you use parentheses.
